items.body: Twenty-five editions after a self-financed experiment in a bunker beneath Wrocław’s Wzgórze Partyzantów, Wrocław Industrial Festival reaches XXV. From 5 to 8 November 2026, Industrial Art brings another four days of industrial, experimental electronics, noise, ritual music, dark ambient and related forms to Stary Klasztor, Sala Gotycka and Sala Witrażowa at ul. Purkyniego 1, with Kino Nowe Horyzonty at Kazimierza Wielkiego 19a/21 also part of the festival infrastructure. The anniversary line-up is appropriately difficult to reduce to one generation or one definition of industrial music. SPKtR / SPK, The Legendary Pink Dots, In The Nursery and Crash Course in Science bring histories reaching back to the formative years of post-industrial and experimental electronic culture. Around them sit artists from power electronics, ritual ambient, rhythm’n’noise, dark folk and contemporary noise, together with two collaborative performances created specifically around meetings between artists. Good to know, because WIF has never functioned well as a nostalgia festival. Its history is built as much on juxtaposition as preservation: originators of industrial culture appear alongside artists who inherited, distorted or ignored its vocabulary completely. From a bunker to the 25th edition The first Wrocław Industrial Festival took place in 2001, founded by Maciej Frett and Arkadiusz Bagiński, both associated with Job Karma. Frett later recalled that the inaugural festival was financed from their own savings and held in the former bunker beneath Wzgórze Partyzantów. The early editions subsequently moved into Sala Gotycka, at that point still an austere, unheated space hardly designed for concerts; organisers have recalled hauling stage equipment through a second-floor window. The first edition brought together ten friendly projects. By 2025, Frett estimated that well over 500 acts had appeared in Wrocław across the festival’s history, ranging from musicians directly involved in establishing industrial music to successive generations of experimental artists. WIF has retained its identity as something broader than a sequence of concerts. Film, audiovisual work, performance, exhibitions, publishing and encounters between artists have repeatedly entered the programme. The festival’s own anniversary reflections have described it as a meeting point for an international community rather than a single-genre event. In 2026, that history arrives at edition number 25. SPKtR / SPK: not simply reopening an archive The most historically important name on the bill is SPKtR / SPK. SPK dates back to Sydney in 1978 and became one of the defining projects of early industrial and noise culture. The present incarnation is centred on Graeme Revell and Robert J. Revell, but its stated purpose is explicitly not to reproduce the old project unchanged. The new SPKtR material is conceived as a continuation of SPK’s experimental logic through contemporary technology and composition. There is an especially strong Wrocław connection here: SPKtR’s own official site describes its November WIF appearance as the point at which the harder, noise-and-rhythm-oriented SPKtR XXX direction will culminate in a major live statement. Robert Revell will additionally perform his own solo material at the festival. His debut solo album, “Torn Remnants of Nobility”, appeared in 2025; he is also part of the current SPK line-up. The Legendary Pink Dots The Legendary Pink Dots bring another extraordinarily long history to Wrocław, although from a very different branch of the underground. The group formed around Edward Ka-Spel and Phil Knight in 1980, subsequently relocating its centre of gravity from Britain to the Netherlands. More than four decades later, the project remains active rather than functioning solely around its catalogue; the official discography continues through 2026. Their psychedelic electronics, experimental song structures and surreal, frequently unstable relationship between pop form and abstraction make them appropriate for WIF: recognisable enough to possess a long-established following, but historically resistant to fitting comfortably into a single scene. In The Nursery: cinema becomes part of the festival One of the most distinctive elements of XXV WIF will come from In The Nursery, the Sheffield project built around twin brothers Klive and Nigel Humberstone, active since 1981. Rather than presenting a conventional concert, In The Nursery will perform their score to Carl Theodor Dreyer’s 1928 silent film “The Passion of Joan of Arc”. The music belongs to the duo’s long-running Optical Music Series, through which they have composed new scores for classic silent cinema; the Joan of Arc score itself was released in 2008. Their official site describes the work as following both the extraordinary intimacy of Renée Falconetti’s close-up performance and the escalating violence of the film’s final sequences. Maciej Frett has specifically identified this as the special cinema concert opening the festival. Crash Course in Science Philadelphia’s Crash Course in Science provide another direct connection to the beginnings of electronic post-punk. Formed in 1979 by art-school students Dale Feliciello, Mallory Yago and Michael Zodorozny, the group developed a raw, percussive electronic sound whose influence subsequently travelled into both industrial music and techno. Placed alongside SPKtR, they make the historical component of XXV WIF more interesting than a simple procession of “industrial pioneers”: these artists arrived at machine music from distinctly different cultural and musical positions. Two collaborations made for the moment Perhaps the most intriguing part of the programme is found in its collaborative projects. N.U. Unruh & Meta Meat will bring together the co-founder and percussionist of Einstürzende Neubauten with French duo Meta Meat, itself built around Phil Von of Von Magnet and Hugues Villette of 2Kilos &More. Meta Meat describe their work as “tribal-industrial”, combining acoustic percussion, physical performance and electronic structures. This is not simply two existing sets placed next to one another. Meta Meat have confirmed that the Wrocław performance with Unruh is a completely new work created specifically for the festival, while Frett has described it as the collaboration’s first public appearance. The second collaboration, Flint Glass & Ah Cama-Sotz, joins Paris-based Gwenn Trémorin and Antwerp-based Herman Klapholz. Their latest album, “The Shadow of the Torturer”, was released by ant-zen in April 2026 and draws on Gene Wolfe’s “The Book of the New Sun”, combining cinematic electronics, ritual elements and darker rhythmic structures. Wrocław matters for this project too: Klapholz has confirmed that WIF will host their first concert together. From rhythmic force to ritual space The rest of the international programme moves across very different understandings of industrial music. Belgium’s Imminent, the project of Olivier Moreau, sits at the harder intersection of sophisticated rhythmic programming, industrial electronics and technoid force. His recent “Mythrality” material continues the combination of intricate rhythm, distorted sequences and colder atmospheric construction that has defined the project. German project Apoptose moves in almost the opposite direction. Active since around the turn of the millennium, its work has long centred on dark ambient, ritual structures and field recording. The 2025 album “Die Zeit und die Dunkelheit” returned explicitly to forests, natural recordings, solitude and slowly unfolding electronic environments. American Control, Thomas Garrison’s long-running project, occupies the territory between power electronics and death industrial, using aggression less as uninterrupted assault than as part of a carefully constructed atmospheric architecture. Finland’s Halo Manash, active since 2003, takes ritual even further. Its recordings draw heavily on drone, elemental field recordings and ceremonial approaches to sound; some releases originate directly from private ritual performances recorded in northern Finland. Belgian Empusae brings another organic and electro-acoustic interpretation of post-industrial music, moving through ritual, ambient, doom and soundtrack-like composition. And Blood and Sun, formed by Luke Tromiczak in 2011, takes the programme into dark folk: voice, strings, percussion and a musical language concerned with myth, spiritual experience and human struggle rather than electronics alone. Robert Revell, PFFFT…! and Espectra Negra Alongside his work in the current SPKtR configuration, Robert Revell will perform separately. His 2025 solo album “Torn Remnants of Nobility” brings together his background across noise, metal, musique concrète and experimental composition. Berlin’s PFFFT…! reaches almost as far back historically as some of the festival’s best-known guests. The project describes itself as an autonomous, constantly mutating body whose first actions date to 1984; its 2025 “Bunkerbeschallung” sits between industrial electronics, noise and what the project itself tags as “miner wave”. Espectra Negra, the Berlin-based project of Mexican artist Verónica Mota, works with ritualistic noise, industrial experimentation and politically charged sound. Her album “Empire” appeared through HANDS and includes contributions from artists including N.U. Unruh. The Polish contingent The Polish side of XXV WIF is equally broad. Opowieść construct performances around noise, mechanical sound, film projection and live visual actions. Their album “Podróż” develops a language strongly associated with movement and train-like mechanical rhythm, while their concerts have been described by the project itself as forms of musical ritual combined with visual performance. Rites of Fall & Fugavit continue their joint audiovisual project. Rites of Fall, created by Bartek Kuszewski, grew from experiments placing religious and folk material into new contexts; with visual artist Fugavit, the collaborative performance has previously appeared under the title “Into the Well”. Warsaw duo Mazut, Paweł Starzec and Michał Turowski, have spent roughly a decade moving between acid, industrial, noise and experimental dance music. Their 2025 “Dirt Collector” slowed the project down toward gritty post-industrial ambience, while the 2026 “Live Collector” documents performances from Wrocław and Kraków. Finally, Gdańsk-based Dystopian Control brings the uncompromising end of the Polish noise underground. The project’s first full-length album, “Nothing Changes the Narrative”, arrived through Zoharum in May 2026, using harsh noise as a foundation while pushing beyond straightforward genre formalism. After the concerts The announced DJ programme is equally substantial: Ancient Methods, Philipp Strobel, Blackdeath 1334 / Francesca, Eric and Paradroid are all currently confirmed. The official festival page has not yet published a complete day-by-day running order, so individual performance times should not be assumed at this stage. Who plays when Thursday, 5 November 2026 – Kino Nowe Horyzonty In The Nursery – live score for Carl Theodor Dreyer’s silent film “The Passion of Joan of Arc” Afterparty: DJ Eric Friday, 6 November 2026 – Gothic Hall The Legendary Pink Dots Crash Course in Science Halo Manash Control Blood and Sun Robert Revell PFFFT…! Afterparty: Ancient Methods & Philipp Strobel Saturday, 7 November 2026 – Gothic Hall SPKtR / SPK N.U. Unruh & Meta Meat Flint Glass & Ah Cama-Sotz Imminent Apoptose Empusae Espectra Negra Afterparty: DJ Blackdeath 1334 Sunday, 8 November 2026 – Sala Witrażowa Opowieść Rites of Fall & Fugavit Mazut Dystopian Control Afterparty: DJ Paradroid Practical information XXV Wrocław Industrial Festival 5-8 November 2026 Main venue: Sala Gotycka / Sala Witrażowa / Stary Klasztor ul. Purkyniego 1, Wrocław Cinema venue: Kino Nowe Horyzonty Kazimierza Wielkiego 19a/21, Wrocław The official Polish ticket page currently marks the four-day pass allocation as sold out. Single-day tickets are available, with the current early-bird period running until 31 August: Thursday 85 PLN, Friday 250 PLN, Saturday 250 PLN and Sunday 85 PLN. Twenty-five editions in, perhaps the most convincing thing about WIF is that its anniversary programme does not attempt to summarise industrial music into a fixed historical style. SPK and Crash Course in Science connect directly with its formative period; In The Nursery bring cinema into the equation; Unruh with Meta Meat and Flint Glass with Ah Cama-Sotz create performances whose history is only beginning; while projects such as Dystopian Control demonstrate that noise and industrial practice are still producing new languages locally. For a festival born in a bunker in 2001, that seems a more appropriate way to mark twenty-five editions than simply looking backwards.

items._cn_summary: 本文报道了弗罗茨瓦夫工业音乐节第二十五届的阵容与历史脉络。音乐节从2001年一个地下掩体中的自发实验起步，发展至今已邀请超过五百组艺术家。纪念版阵容跨越数代，既有SPKtR/SPK、The Legendary Pink Dots等早期工业与实验电子文化的重要名字，也有权力电子、仪式氛围、节奏噪音、暗黑民谣及当代噪音等不同方向的实践者。文章特别指出SPKtR并非简单复刻旧作，而是延续SPK的实验逻辑进行当代重构；音乐节还设置了两场围绕艺术家相遇而生的合作表演。整体策划强调不同代际与语汇之间的并置和碰撞，而非怀旧式回顾，同时保留电影、视听、行为、展览等非纯音乐内容，延续其作为国际社群聚集点的定位。

items.body: The Brussels project alarm!systemen released its self-titled debut album on the Belgian label Antibody on July 31, 2026. Jorne Leurs wrote, played and sang all ten tracks, which mix minimal synthpop lines with cold wave drum machines and Dutch and English lyrics. Yannick Franck mastered the record and Yesse Hoedemaekers supplied the artwork. It is out digitally on Bandcamp at 24-bit resolution; no physical edition has been pressed. alarm!systemen by alarm!systemen What alarm!systemen collected on the debut album The album is an assembly rather than a studio session. Leurs describes it as material gathered over six years: “alarm!systemen is a project that was built over many years and originally meant as an audio diary, meant just to process certain events in my life through the lens of my favorite musical genres since childhood. From a very young age, I was inspired by the soundtrack of both the glitter and gloom of the 80s. My first self-titled release features tracks, cassette recordings, and improvisations made between 2019 and 2024.” That span shows in the running order, which moves between short pop shapes and long-form pieces. The ten tracks are “Kapot” (4:48), “Answer Me” (6:04), “BURN” (4:00), “Comple X” (5:37), “Dance With Me” (3:56), “Eindeloos” (8:16), “Fade To Dust” (4:03), “Goes Again” (6:34), “Three” (5:15) and “Void” (7:14). Four of them pass the six-minute mark, and “Eindeloos” is the longest at over eight minutes. Antibody describes the record as existential synthpop and cold wave. No official video has been released and the album is not on Spotify. About Antibody and alarm!systemen alarm!systemen has no earlier release history. This album is its first published work, and Leurs has not documented other projects. What is on record is the account he gives on the release page: the material began as private processing and was never conceived as an album. Antibody operates out of Brussels and is run by Yannick Franck, who records as RAUM. Its first release, Damon Raum’s “Tantale”, appeared on December 4, 2020, and the catalogue has since grown to around fifty titles. The label describes itself as “a label specializing in de(con)structed forms of Techno, New Wave, EBM, Industrial, Dark Ambient, Sound Art, Metal and Noise”. Franck is a Liège-born sound artist based in Brussels whose own work runs through the projects Y.E.R.M.O. with Xavier Dubois, Orphan Swords with Pierre de Mûelenaere, and Figure Section with Olivia Carrère. He also founded the Idiosyncratics label and scored the 2023 film “The Belgian Wave”. Side-Line has followed Antibody since its early years, covering Hypnoskull launches all new single ‘TMKF’ on the Belgian Antibody label in May 2022, Lebanese electro project Maltash lands new EP on Antibody label in August 2022 and Brussels based label Antibody to release Jean Baudrillard inspired ‘Fatal Strategies’ compilation in March 2023. The alarm!systemen album sits at the synthpop end of that catalogue rather than the techno and noise end.

items.body: New Zealand artist Abby Helasdottir has been active for many years; she released her debut work twenty-five years ago, and many more have followed since. In recent years, the project has been primarily associated with the Winter-Light label. “Níu Kom Ek Heima Fyr Niflhel Neðan” serves as the final installment of a trilogy that began in 2021 with “Ár Var Alda.” The work revolves around the imagery of nine underworlds, evoking a chthonic reflection of the Norse cosmos akin to Kabbalistic mysticism. Musically, the theme translates into an exquisitely detailed production featuring an impressive sonic canvas. Amidst the myriad sound manipulations, effects, and field recordings, the artist crafts a sophisticated composition that ensnares the listener in an imaginary web. While the atmosphere does not always fully come across—likely due to the sheer scale of the sonic arsenal—one quickly senses the work’s darker side. Although I have known Gydja to experiment less in the past, this remains a remarkable sonic experience from an artist who clearly approaches her work from a unique perspective. The genre sits somewhere between Dark-Ambient, Cinematic, and pure Experimental music. The final track delivers a true apotheosis, blending quiet Tribal elements with a magnificent Eastern atmosphere. If you are looking for a breath of fresh air within established genres like Dark-Ambient and Cinematic music, this work is certainly worth a listen. (Rating:7½). Listen to “Heidthornir”: Heidthornir by Gydja About Gydja Gydja is the dark ambient project of Abby Helasdottir, a musician and graphic artist based in Wellington, New Zealand. The project name is an Old Norse word for priestess, and Helasdottir has described the music as dark ambience for dark goddesses. Alongside her own recordings she has produced cover artwork for a range of releases, including titles issued by Cold Spring. The project dates back to the start of the 2000s, with the CDR “The Darkness Gathering” appearing on Mediatrix in 2001. Later solo work includes “Umbilicus Maris” in 2007 and “Helchemy” in 2009. Helasdottir was one of the artists on the Cryo Chamber collaborative album “Nyarlathotep” in 2016. She also records as Bestia Astrum. More recent releases have come through the Dutch label Winter-Light, which issued the trilogy completed by this album. It opened with “Ár Var Alda” in 2021, built around the primordial void Ginnungagap, and continued with “Þjóðáar Fnæstu Eitri”, which took the eleven-fold river Élivágar as its subject. The closing title is drawn from the Old Norse poem “Vafþrúðnismál”. “Níu Kom Ek Heima Fyr Niflhel Neðan” was released on 8 May 2026 on digital and CD. Helasdottir recorded and produced the album at Ultrasound between 2024 and 2025, handled the graphic design, and Robin Storey mastered it.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Gydja三部曲的终章，围绕九个地下世界的意象展开，将北欧宇宙观与卡巴拉神秘主义相映照。音乐上以精密的声音设计为核心，大量运用声音操控、效果处理与田野录音，构建出层次丰富的声响画布。整体风格介于黑暗氛围、电影配乐与纯粹实验音乐之间，最终曲融合了部落节奏与东方氛围，形成全作的升华点。乐评指出，尽管庞大的声音素材有时使氛围传达不够充分，但作品仍展现出艺术家独特的视角与成熟的制作能力。

items.body: On Alpine Variations, Venetian-based composer, guitarist, and field recorder Enrico Coniglio treks towards an ambient apex. The peak of the mountain glimmers from afar, slowly revealing its crystalline beauty the closer he gets. On this strikingly-sublime record, Coniglio’s ambient music is able to dissipate any remaining clouds to uncover a majestic sight. The ascent is long, but it is clearly worth the journey. The euphoria of reaching the top, the victory that comes with the conquest, is contained within its vapours of ambient. On top of that, there is an amazing sense of scale, along with a deep respect for the mountain. It is also a sharp reminder of one’s mortality. Atmosphere and the environment are placed like a flag at the tip of the music, which becomes increasingly icy and frost-bitten, and its dull, gleaming harmonies produce a lambent light. Coniglio has been advancing along these musical paths for years, exploring the sounds of the Earth and transcribing their vibrations; the care behind the music, along with its attention to detail, immediately shines through. It is clear that he has a love for the mountains. Although they are imposing, dominating the landscape and knifing through the sky, the music is more in line with awe than fear, although there is a healthy dose of that, too. Each piece climbs closer to the top, the ascent marked in stages, like checkpoints along the way, and the music is forever building on its foundations, although its footsteps are quick to disappear in the snow. Dense textures and thin ambient winds whistle along the mountain, which is evocative of a spiritual and mental journey as much as it is a physical one. Endurance is essential if one wishes to reach the tip of the peak, and there is something of an inner fight, a push to continue on, to never give up, encased within the ambient textures. The continual shifts of its ice and the thunders of a distant avalanche are a reminder of its constant danger. Like the mountain itself, it is breath-taking music, equally calming and spectacular. Alpine Variations by Enrico Coniglio www.dronarivm.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以环境音乐与实地录音为基础，构建了一段从山脚到山顶的听觉攀登之旅。乐评指出，音乐通过密集的织体与稀薄的风声纹理，营造出高山地带的寒冷与空旷感，同时将物理攀登与精神旅程相互映射。每一首曲目都像登山途中的阶段性标记，在持续铺展的和声与细微声响变化中逐步推进，但足迹又迅速被风雪掩盖，暗示着征服与消逝的并存。作曲家对山脉的敬畏体现在对声音细节的精心处理上，远处雪崩的轰鸣与冰层的不断移动提醒着自然的危险与人类的脆弱。整体上，作品在平静与壮阔之间取得平衡，既是对地理景观的描绘，也是对内心耐力的考验，适合专注于声音层次与氛围演变的聆听者。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以俄罗斯绑架乌克兰儿童事件为背景，混合传统歌曲与原创作品，由乌克兰和加拿大两组全女性乐手演绎，包含班杜拉、双陶笛等乐器，以女声和弓弦乐器为主。乐评人刻意先不读背景说明直接聆听，认为音乐本身在声乐和器乐层面都相当有力，随后读到歌词翻译时深受触动。《Foreign Land》改编自传统歌曲，用母亲送女儿远赴异乡的意象映射被掳儿童的处境，演唱温柔；《Rusalka》则由Alina Kuzma领唱，转向激烈尖锐，呼应神话中自然精灵的原始力量。专辑兼具抒情与张力，以传统音乐形式承载当代创伤记忆，文化视角独特。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦圣多美和普林西比1970-80年代的Puxa音乐，延续第一辑的挖掘路线。Puxa融合了安哥拉、莫桑比克等葡语非洲前殖民地的节奏，并吸收加勒比海地区的merengue、kompas、soukouss、benga等元素，形成复杂而富有律动的舞曲风格。专辑收录15首作品，展现多把吉他交织、主唱与和声应答的结构，人声融入旋律框架，节奏组在部分曲目中抽离或重现，营造出绵长而热烈的舞池氛围。尽管当地音乐场景规模有限，这些录音仍呈现出丰富的创作活力，也印证了Puxa舞曲在历史禁令下的顽强生命力。作为非洲音乐黄金时代的记录，它兼具文化史料与听觉享受的双重价值。

items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,
Songs of Compassion
is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: Dorothy Moskowitz携新项目United States of Alchemy回归，与Francesco Paolo Paladino和Luca Chino Ferrari合作推出《Songs of Compassion》。专辑以非线性的前卫作曲为核心，钢琴在前后景中交错、错位，搭配弦乐、木管与合成器音色，构建出疏离而富有冥想性的声响空间。歌词兼具诗意与当代政治锋芒，如《Pale Wanderer》探讨威权体制下的共谋，《Charlottesville》直接指涉新纳粹事件，延续1960年代抗议歌曲传统，同时融入对死亡与宇宙位置的哲思。Moskowitz的人声如方法派演员般浸入文本，旋律不循传统和声逻辑，而是随词语意义起伏，钢琴则扮演类似希腊合唱团的评论角色。整体音乐在令人迷失的和谐运动中，挑战西方调性习惯，呈现出更古老、更遥远的声音叙事，适合偏好实验、当代古典与政治表达融合的听众。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)

items._cn_summary: Alison Cotton的新作延续了她一贯难以归类的创作路径，将民谣、前卫音乐与宗教感融合，并以中提琴、簧风琴、锤扬琴、钢琴等乐器构建出朦胧而静谧的氛围。专辑多采用即兴演奏与单次录音完成，带有近乎神秘的聆听体验，如《I Am!》为约翰·克莱尔的诗歌配上超验旋律，在持续嗡鸣中流动。同名中心曲目《Sprigs of Heather》从中世纪圣乐般的开头过渡到钢琴主导的舒缓旋律，精致而动人。整张专辑也是对其父亲的纪念，尤其《The Final Harvest》以庄重而温柔的笔触描绘父亲最后一次造访他钟爱的菜园，情感沉潜于音符之间。光与暗、失落与慰藉交织，作品超越类型边界，既具挑战性又充满感染力。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)
items.label: Analog Africa
items._genre: afro-funk / world music / vodun rhythm / congolese rumba / cuban son
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了贝宁传奇乐队 Orchestre Poly-Rythmo 与歌手 Antoine Dougbé 在 1977-1982 年间的作品。Dougbé 被称为“魔鬼总理”，是伏都教仪式音乐的实践者，其音乐核心源自一种名为 Cavacha 的腿部拍打节奏，由鼓手 Belobi Meridjo 根据火车韵律发展而来。与乐队其他合辑相比，此辑更明显地受到古巴 son 音乐影响，同时融入刚果伦巴与合成器音色，呈现出 70 年代末至 80 年代初非洲流行乐的过渡样貌。吉他的塑料光泽、密集踩镲节奏与合成器铺底交织，人声呼应保持经典质感，展现了非洲本土节奏与拉丁、刚果元素的深度混合。Analog Africa 的发掘让这批短暂而强烈的录音得以重见天日，具有鲜明的西非地域文化与历史价值。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: 塔科·托基以废料和零碎物件自制乐器，却在校准音准和录音质感上达到很高准确度。作品延续首张专辑的拼贴式世界音乐路线，将东欧单簧管传统旋律、拉丁打击乐、非洲节奏与中东调式纳入松散而灵活的即兴框架。开篇曲中的拟声喊叫与低音管形成戏剧性对话；标题曲以马林巴琴配合铃铛与镲片，在节拍之上展开爵士化的独奏；长笛在桑巴和中东风格曲目中分别呈现温暖与迷幻色彩。自制乐器并非噱头，而是与作曲和演奏深度绑定，让每首曲目既有手工质感又不失专业控制。整张专辑在幽默与严肃之间保持平衡，提醒听者音乐可以脱离昂贵器材而存在。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了Camilla Hole Trio对挪威民间音乐的探索，但相比前作的科幻感更显沉静与落地。开场曲《Springleik》以挪威西部舞蹈曲调为基底，萨克斯主奏搭配低音提琴与鼓的节奏支撑，随后合成器与电颤琴的叠录逐渐展开音色层次。三人的角色并不固定，低音提琴手接过旋律与萨克斯齐奏，鼓手则拓展节奏空间，整体氛围从民间舞曲转向自由即兴。作品在传统素材与爵士即兴之间游走，既保留民间旋律的辨识度，又通过乐器角色互换和电子音色注入当代实验感，体现了北欧爵士融合领域特有的克制与开放性。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由瑞典小提琴家Mats Edén与挪威音乐家Tellef Kvifte、Knut Kvifte Nesheim组成的三重奏录制，以非传统方式诠释北欧传统舞曲。他们并未延续舞曲的伴奏功能，而是将其转化为类似室内乐的亲密对话，三人沉浸于细微的声响互动中，探索曲调背后隐藏的神秘与暗流。Tellef Kvifte以sjfløyte（竖笛）担任主要旋律，Mats Edén的小提琴提供纹理化伴奏，Knut Kvifte Nesheim则以打击乐点缀，整体呈现出即兴而碎片化的结构。开篇曲《Fossgrimen》取材于挪威水精灵传说，暗示了音乐中潜藏的阴郁维度；瑞典波尔斯卡舞曲《Polska from Per Myhr》则从齐奏逐渐瓦解至静默。专辑在传统民谣与实验即兴之间找到了独特的平衡，值得一听。

items.body: Berlin art-pop and indietronica artist Gene Sophia Bogolepov release “Slow Down Your Burning” on 3 September 2026 through MYCELM, the label and archive Bogolepov run from the same city. It is the first single from “Dråma”, a nine-track album set for 11 November 2026, and it carries the darkwave and experimental edges that have run through the project since its move to Germany. The album will be sold through Bandcamp, Qobuz and the MYCELM platform. It will not appear on Spotify in full. MYCELM states that the omission follows the artist’s ideological beliefs, so the album is being kept off the largest streaming service by choice rather than by a licensing gap. “Dråma” was assembled by a small group. Diego Ferri handled guitars, production and engineering, Volodymyr Nestryga played drums and percussion, Dimitri Klochkov contributed guitars, bass and synths, and Scout Hansen co-wrote. Piano parts came from Andrian Lebedev, who died in 2021. How ‘Dråma’ began, four days before the invasion On 20 February 2022, four days before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Bogolepov was in the studio with Scout Hansen, working while anxious about what was coming. “Serpent Song” came out of that session, written from inside the mind of a psychopath, and the rest of the album grew around it over the four years that followed. MYCELM describes the result as “an album about faith, justice, violence, and what happens when catastrophe becomes ordinary.” The 2017 song “Mother Russia” drew enough hostility in Russia to push the artist into exile, and the move to Berlin reset the project. “Art Brut” followed in 2021. Onstage the current line-up is a duo: Bogolepov with Diego Ferri, a Berlin musician and sound engineer who played guitar for and produced the Canadian lo-fi act Michelle Gurevich, and whose other credits take in BBC1 and work with Martin Bisi, the New York producer behind records by Sonic Youth and Swans. Recent appearances include Ms Artville Festival in Hamburg in 2021, Noorderzon Festival in Groningen and WORM in Rotterdam in 2022, Berghain in 2024 and LARK in Berlin in 2025. MYCELM has also submitted the album to Wave-Gotik-Treffen 2027. No 2027 WGT line-up has been announced, so no booking is confirmed. About Gene Sophia Bogolepov Gene Sophia Bogolepov grew up in a working-class household in Saint Petersburg, surrounded by family instruments, and first performed in 2003. The early electropunk project T-Lazarus came out of that period, followed by the electro-rock band Gender ID, which played across Russia and Europe on bills with Ladytron, Placebo, Editors, Sparks and Apparat Band. Two further projects, Dukes of Betelgeuse and Ego Collider, ran alongside them. In 2013 Bogolepov adopted the name 1314 and turned the work towards living with HIV, anxiety and queer isolation. The 2017 anti-authoritarian song “Mother Russia” produced a backlash that led to exile, and Berlin became the base from then on. “Art Brut” arrived in 2021, and the catalogue collected on the MYCELM platform now runs from “Ultrawhite” and “Home Kids & Bathroom Romance” through “[bodies] EP”, “Deviant Comedy”, the 1314 LP, “Art Brut”, “Long Awaited Silence Of Mind (坂本龍一に捧げる)”, the “Titanium” EP and the “Art Brut (Mycelium Edition)” reissue. MYCELM itself began as Mycelium, a paywalled discography archive, and relaunched under its current name in February 2026 as what Bogolepov describes as an archive, community and label for underground and unsigned artists, most of them queer. It publishes as Mycelm Records and Mycelm Publishing out of Berlin, and it now handles both “Slow Down Your Burning” and “Dråma”.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以暗潮和实验声响为骨架，记录了创作者在俄国入侵乌克兰前四天那段焦虑时光。《Dråma》由小型团队在四年间逐步搭建，吉他、鼓、贝斯、合成器与已故钢琴师录制的钢琴段落交织成关于信仰、正义、暴力以及灾难常态化主题的九首作品。创作者成长于圣彼得堡工人阶级家庭，早期有电子朋克和电气摇滚经历，因政治表达被迫流亡柏林，作品中延续了对身份、HIV焦虑和酷儿孤绝议题的探讨。录制团队成员参与过加拿大lo-fi艺人制作，并与Sonic Youth、Swans的纽约制作人有交集。专辑选择不登陆Spotify，仅通过Bandcamp、Qobuz及自有平台MYCELM发行，体现出对意识形态的坚持。多年来在Berghain、WORM等地下场地的演出经历，以及对Wave-Gotik-Treffen的投递，进一步确立了其艺术暗潮与地下电子的定位。

items.body: Buenos Aires project Sektor Voltage released “En otra dimensión” on June 6, 2026, an eight-track fourth album that mixes electronic body music rhythms with post-punk guitars and coldwave synths. Nicolás Pomilio, who has run the project on his own since 2020, self-released it in digital form. The album is his first to build the songs around guitar rather than around the drum machine. Pomilio describes the shift as a return to what the project was for, not a departure from it: “En otra dimensión (2026) is born: the soul slips beyond the visible, traveling through astral realms. Driven by a motorik pulse, post-punk guitars, futuristic synths, and Nicolás’s cavernous voice, the tracks create dark, danceable atmospheres that hypnotize and transport. Returning to reality is up to the listener.” The eight tracks are “Hojas Negras”, “En otra dimensión”, “In den Verborgenen Wäldern”, “Látigo”, “Cerebro reptil”, “Dornen und Splitter”, “Tu propia sombra” and “Ilusión”. Two carry German titles, and both point at the same reference: the German dark scene of the 1980s, which Pomilio names alongside the old Frankfurt sound and Belgian new beat. He recorded the album on a Zoom R8 portastudio. Drums came from a Kawai R50e and bass from a Korg Monologue, both sequenced over MIDI, with a Yamaha QY10 bass patch used on “Látigo”. Korg Volca FM and Microkorg synths were played live, and percussion, backing vocals and strings were added by hand from a Casio SA keyboard. Guitars and vocals went into Ableton through the Zoom R8’s effects, and the master was finished there too. En otra dimensión by Sektor Voltage The first single, “In den Verborgenen Wäldern”, came with a video directed by Damian Bentrón and Marcelo Moiola and filmed in Rafael Calzada, in the southern Greater Buenos Aires belt, in May 2026. It follows Pomilio alone through open country while the track’s machinery runs underneath. About Sektor Voltage Sektor Voltage is the solo project of Nicolás Pomilio, a producer, guitarist and singer from the southern zone of Greater Buenos Aires, Argentina. He started it in 2020 as an experimental sonic search after working as a DJ and producer in techno, new beat, EBM and darkwave, and turned it into a dark, danceable live set drawn from 1980s sources. Three albums preceded the current one, all self-released and all eight tracks long. “Amor a mi negra lista” arrived on May 14, 2023, followed by “Animal en extinción” on February 11, 2024 and “Oscura noche del alma” on January 28, 2025. Across them Pomilio worked through darkwave, EBM and industrial textures, naming Kraftwerk, Depeche Mode, early Ministry and Front 242 as the starting points. “Oscura noche del alma” also carries a cover of Youth Code‘s “Avengement” and the track “Sexo social” featuring Neuromi. Pomilio has said he felt something was missing after that run, so he made the guitar his main instrument and reworked his voice around the hybrid it produced. The reference points changed with it: post-punk, coldwave and 1980s darkwave, from The Cure and Opéra de Nuit to Malaria!, X-Mal Deutschland and Siekiera. “En otra dimensión” is the first Sektor Voltage record built from that starting point, and it leans on coldwave, goth and post-punk where the earlier releases leaned on EBM and industrial.
items._cn_summary: 阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯单人项目Sektor Voltage的第四张专辑首次以吉他为核心构建歌曲，延续了电子机体音乐节奏与冷潮合成器的融合路线。制作方面，鼓机与贝斯通过MIDI序列器编排，合成器现场演奏，人声与吉他经Zoom R8端口录音室进入Ableton完成母带，整体呈现八十年代德国暗黑场景、法兰克福之声与比利时new beat的影响。专辑收录八首作品，其中两首以德语命名，暗指欧洲暗黑传统。作为独立自发行的拉丁美洲地下电子作品，其将后朋克吉他切入EBM框架的处理方式，展现了南美场景对欧洲暗黑遗产的重新诠释。

items.body: Grief has a strange relationship with distance. The dead may be unreachable in any practical sense, yet the mind keeps inventing routes toward them: dreams, remembered voices, photographs, coincidences that briefly acquire the weight of messages. Frankie Rose describes that nocturnal search with the rueful humour of someone who knows how unreliable the equipment can be. Her latest single, Return To Dust, has intense emotional gravity. Drawn from Rose’s forthcoming album Hila, the song treats grief as a condition in which perception grows unstable, opening possibilities that daylight tends to dismiss. Rose’s voice hangs high in the arrangement, cool and clear against drums and synthesizers with considerable physical force beneath them. There are echoes of Enya’s suspended grandeur, PJ Harvey’s severity, the private ache of Cat Power, and the voluptuous gloom of Portishead; elsewhere, the guitar and vocal textures recall Cocteau Twins and the ceremonial grandeur of Siouxsie and the Banshees. Rose has spent much of the past fifteen years refining her ability to make scale and solitude coexist. On Return To Dust, enormous spaces seem to open around a voice that remains remarkably intimate. The production has breadth without sacrificing detail, with each layer contributing to an impression of drifting farther from familiar coordinates while carrying something painfully terrestrial along for the ride. “In my dreams I travel the cosmos and the astral realm looking for ones I’ve lost,” says Frankie Rose. “But I’m a pretty bad receiver, and I am pretty sure I keep missing what they’re trying to tell me.” The self-directed video literalizes Rose’s celestial preoccupations with a playful montage that sends her wandering through the cosmos. She floats among stars and planetary vistas, appearing less like an astronaut conquering unknown territory than a traveller amusing herself while attempting an impossible form of correspondence. The homemade theatricality is crucial. Rather than turning bereavement into solemn science fiction, Rose permits herself whimsy, introducing the peculiar comedy of trying to locate the dead somewhere beyond the visible universe. The video’s cosmic scenery therefore feels less like escape than an extension of mourning itself. Loss can make ordinary reality seem insufficient, sending the imagination searching for some hidden frequency on which absence might become communication. Rose understands the absurdity in that desire and allows it to remain absurd without diminishing its emotional force. Somewhere beyond the planets, perhaps, a message is being transmitted. For now, she is still turning the dial. Watch the video for Return To Dust below: The tension between wonder and uncertainty runs throughout Frankie Rose’s forthcoming album Hila. “Hila is a record about loss,” she says. “What persists beyond the range of ordinary perception? The place mourning keeps returning to — not quite transcendence, not quite doubt. The edge of what we can see.” Self-produced in Rose’s home studio after extensive touring with The Jesus & Mary Chain and Swervedriver, the album also features drummer Justin Welch, known for his work with Elastica and Lush. Its darker passages draw from the esoteric menace of later Coil, the bodily propulsion of Skinny Puppy, and the otherworldly pop vocabulary associated with Cocteau Twins. Yet Return To Dust suggests that Rose’s fascination with these references has become increasingly personal. Genre provides the architecture; bereavement supplies the strange new physics. Listen to Return To Dust below and order the single here. Hila is out September 18 via Born Losers Records worldwide outside the EU and UK, and Night School Records in the EU and UK. Order vinyl here. items._cn_summary: Frankie Rose 新单 Return to Dust 以悲恸为内核，将哀悼转化为一场宇宙尺度的内在探索。制作层面，鼓与合成器构筑出具有物理冲击力的低频基底，人声则悬浮其上，保持冷冽与亲密的平衡。文中提及的影响谱系横跨 Enya 的悬浮壮阔、PJ Harvey 的冷峻严苛、Cat Power 的私密痛感、Portishead 的丰沛阴郁、Cocteau Twins 的吉他织体以及 Siouxsie and the Banshees 的仪式感，体现出明确的暗潮与梦幻流行取向。Rose 对'尺度与孤独共存'的掌控是十五年磨砺的结果，庞大空间感与细节并存。歌词与自导 MV 以幽默消解悲伤的庄严，将天人永隔的失落呈现为一场在星体间寻找讯号的荒诞通讯实验，悲喜交织而不削弱情感重量。专辑 Hila 围绕丧失与超感知展开，是独立厂牌发行的高度个人化作品。

items.body: Top PickThe Night Eternal – Cold Velvet (Amorphis-ised goth-metal/rock)There are two bands that immediately spring to mind when pressing play on Cold Velvet. The first is Unto Others, whose similar retro aesthetic and goth rock posturing make them an obvious point of comparison. The second, less expected and ultimately more successful spice of The Night Eternal's ingredients is Amorphis. It's not only that vocalist Ricardo Baum resembles Tomi Jousten both sonically and physically, but the wiry lead melodies and ambient textures supplied by guitarists Rob Richter and Henry Käseberg also readily bring to mind that band's mid-period. Indeed, Cold Velvet could be something Amorphis had come up with themselves, had the chosen to pursue the darker, more alt-metal leaning sound of 2006's Eclipse, rather than gradually reverting to progressive, folk-tinged melodeath of the albums that followed.Whereas Unto others put me off with their overcompensating aesthetics and affected vocals, The Night eternal ooze an effortless cool that comes through in their music as well. There's a sleek suaveness that characterises the aptly and enticingly named Cold Velvet, that makes every moment of its sullen transmission completely compelling and instantly memorable, even if its perhaps lacking a bit of the more forceful metallic textures that have made both Amorphis and Unto others more recognisable. If The Night Eternal can mix a bit more metallic grit into their sound, then we could truly be looking at the next goth metal juggernaut. items.body: “Desilusión” catches the moment an expectation loses its shape and reality takes over. It carries the weight of something that did not go as hoped, and Cisco Pema keeps it that way, without tipping into melodrama. The song moves past that first letdown into acceptance, the turn from expecting something of someone to understanding you needed to stop. It makes that process an intimate song about learning to let go. An Argentine bassist, singer and producer, Pema grew up in Buenos Aires and was on stage from childhood. He moved to Austria for a jazz and improvisation diploma at the Bruckner University, worked as a bassist, composer and producer, then settled in Berlin, where he launched a solo career in 2016. His songs run South American forms through jazz harmony, with traditional and contemporary rhythms underneath. His run of records takes in the self-titled Cisco Pema (2018), Otra realidad (2021) and Tres de Oro (2023), which turns towards rock and pop rock, alongside the 2017 EP Tu Casa Es Mi Casa, made with Munich reggae band Jamaram, that moves between Latin, reggae and dub. items._cn_summary: 《Desilusión》将目光投向期望落空、现实逐渐显形的临界时刻，并让情绪从最初的失望自然过渡到接纳。Cisco Pema 的处理克制而内敛，没有把失落渲染成戏剧化宣泄，而是把‘不再对某人抱有期待’的内心转变写成一首关于放手的私密之歌。作为阿根廷出生的贝斯手与制作人，他的音乐带有南美节奏的呼吸感，又在和声与旋律的推进上显出学院派训练的控制力。作品在个人叙事与声音细节之间取得平衡，值得留意的是它如何用层层铺展的情绪变化带动听者，而非依赖歌词直白煽情。

items.body:
Daria Lourd (Bored Lord) + her wife, vocalist Jaelynn Walls = DARLYNN on their debut shot of Jersey club meets ‘90s R&B, woozy garage house and vintage psych-funk flavours.

"Darlynn is an Oakland-based duo composed of Daria Lourd (aka Bored Lord) and her wife, vocalist Jaelynn Walls. Dyke Den is a lesbian love story about two creative individuals finding each other and themselves through effusive and contemplative sonic avenues. Created in their home over the course of two years, this album speaks to the journey of Daria and Jaelynn’s romantic relationship as well as their evolving combined creative impulses.

On Dyke Den, Darlynn display their influences – from Janet Jackson and Sly & the Family Stone, to Frankie Knuckles and Larry Levan – in a sophisticated, fully realized, and overtly queered fashion. Joyous dancefloor moments are abundant. Tracks like “Make Yr Move” and “Like A Summer” celebrate deep house vibes ala Alleviated Records, while sultry R&B moves are flexed on “Girl 2 Girl” and “Alright With Me.” But longing and yearning exist within this joyous arc, and the question arises: “How can I get you to love me?” More than an idealistic narrative of girl meets they/them, Dyke Den paints a portrait of love in all its multifaceted moments: the bids for commitment, the stagnation of years going by, the wormholes of desire. Yet the album maintains its thesis of hope. The sweet, layered harmonies of closing song “Love Letter” display the power of life partnership: “My whole life is a love letter to you.” Dyke Den features artwork by Hailee Va in a sleeve designed by Eloise Shir-Juen Leigh. Darlynn’s final declaration, “We are all creatures of desire, completely built for love.”s"

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以Jersey club和R&B为基底，融入车库浩室与迷幻放克元素，在家庭录音室历时两年完成。作品以女同性恋爱情故事为主线，展现两位创作者从相遇到共同成长的过程，同时受Janet Jackson、Sly & the Family Stone等影响，既有欢快的舞池律动，也有深情的渴望表达。专辑在欢愉与沉思之间取得平衡，结尾曲以层叠和声呈现伴侣间的承诺，整体呈现出细腻且具个人色彩的情感叙事。

items.body:
Michael J. Blood lends two rugged, tumping takes to Intertoto’s rudely groggy beatdown house

‘If I Take You Home’ is the first cut from London’s Intertoto since his well received album ‘Thermal Shadow’ (2023) and continues down a midnight path of mid-tempo, strutting beatdown roughly guided by likes of NWAQ and Kassel Mosse.

MJB steps it up a gear or two in a ‘Walk of Shame Mix’ built from woodcut kicks and gritty sampler revs plus additional vox like Martin Rev just walked in the room and did a Travolta “huh?”, plus a banging ‘Morning After Mix’ cloaked in muffled party noise and prompting jelly legs back to the ‘floor.
items._cn_summary: Intertoto的新单曲延续其2023年专辑《Thermal Shadow》以来的午夜中速beatdown house路线，受NWAQ与Kassel Mosse等风格影响。Michael J. Blood为此制作了两个混音版本：'Walk of Shame Mix'以木刻般底鼓和粗粝的采样推进，人声如同Martin Rev突然闯入；'Morning After Mix'则被闷响的派对噪音包裹，营造出令人腿软回到舞池的律动。整体在舞池节拍中注入脏砺质感和即兴气息，适合偏好地下电子与实验舞曲的听众。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是现代roots reggae乐队的第五作，主唱塞内加尔出生的背景为音乐注入独特文化视角。其嗓音与唱腔带有鲍勃·马利式的根源气质，同时以灵魂乐式的细腻咬字和情感铺陈，让人联想到丹尼斯·布朗等经典歌手。中段之后，演唱方式逐渐突破传统雷鬼的框架，如水渗纸般自然变形。声音制作上，作品更深入地回溯1980年前后的roots reggae传统，却不局限于复古，而是将布鲁斯、灵魂乐与非洲R&B元素有机融合，以当代听觉重新审视雷鬼与非洲音乐之间的血脉联系。整体听感兼具根源厚度与流动感，是roots reggae在全球化语境下的一种发展型表达。

items.body: The Proms concert on August 10 was presented by an orchestra consisting of students from the Juilliard School in New York and the Royal Academy of Music, conducted by Esa-Pekka Salonen, with Vilde Frang as violin soloist. The program consisted of works by three of the most imporant composers of the early twentieth century, Igor Stravinsky (Symphony in Three Movements, 1942-45), Alban Berg (Violin Concerto, 1935, and Béla Bartok, Concerto for Ochestra, 1943-rev 1945). The Stravinsky, written after his move to California is a reaction not only to the ongoing world war (the program notes quoted Stravinsky in one of his conversation books with Robert Craft saying that the third movement was a ‘musical reaction to the newsreels and documentaries that I had seen of goose-stepping soldiers”) but his relations with business in his new home (the second movement began as sketches for possible music for the movie of Werfel’s The Song of Bernadette). This listener, on hearing the first movement, was reminded of a quote from W. H. Auden that sometimes the mature poet will have need to imitate himself, since it seemed to be a perfect imitation of a Stravinsky piece. The Berg Concerto, on the other hand is completely first hand, and genuine. The performance was somewhat lacking in terms of its shaping and balancing. The Albert Hall can be especially difficult for a soloist in terms of playing to the hall and that is especially true of the Berg. For this listener the most convincing performance was of the Bartok Concerto for Orchestra, It is certainly the most familiar of the three pieces, and that familiarity can cause it to be somewhat taken for granted. This performance made one realize what a very very good piece it is, and brought out all its strengths and, in fact, all of Bartok’s strengths. If one needed a comparison between a world class, absolutely beyond reproach student orchestra and a thoroughly ‘grown-up,” “professional” one, it was provided the next night by the Los Angeles Philharmonic. Conducted by its artistic director, Gustavo Dudamel. The concert began with a staggeringly beautiful performance of the Beethoven Pastorale Symphony, full of beauty of tone, nuance, color, and clarity of articulation and was followed by the first part of the ballet Dante by Thomas Adès, Inferno, the performance of which was equally brilliant. Dante is a score for a ballet by choreographer Wayne McGregory, a long-time collaborator of Adés. In the first part which was what was played on this concert, Adés uses music of Lizst in much the same way the Stravinsky used the music of Pergolesi in his ballet Pulcinella. Various works of Lizst constitute the content of the work, and can be quoted and orchestrated, but also can be used as source material for music less directly related to specific pieces. The first twelve sections of the work, tracing the circles of hell, build energy leading up to the rousing (described by Venn as showstopping) the Theives, which the audience assumed was the finale, and cheered enthuisatically when it ended. However there was a final circle, Satan, depicting Lucifer trapped in ice, which brought the piece to a conclusion which might well be described as bone chilling. All of the work is brilliantly conceived and realized, with fabulous orchestration, and awesome instrumental writing. To be completely honest, it left this listener a little cold. The audience loved it. The concert by the Los Angeles Philharmonic was followed by a late-night Prom given by Evelyn Glennie, the BBC Singers, and the Fantasia Orchestra, conducted by Tom Fetherstonehaugh. There wass also sign language interpretation by Sean Chandler. There was a very wide range of types and styles of music; Glennie, in an interview in the program, described the programming strategy as being like ‘walking through different rooms of human experience.’ The program started with John Coltrane’s Welcome, followed by It Don’t Mean a Thing by Duke Ellington. It went on from there to include music by Morton Feldman (some of Rothko Chapel), Caroline Shaw, Dvorak, Vaughan Williams (Serenade to Music), and Radiohead, including, along the way a piece by Glennie and Philip Sheppard, a first Prom performance of Sandman’s Castle by Vincent Ho, and a first performance of The Wood Pigeon by Héloïse Werner, commissioned by the BBC for this concert, ending up with Meredith Monk’s Panda Chant. The playing and singing by all concerned was wonderful and engaging and the whole experience was refreshing and exhilarating. The post BBC Proms —Stravinsky, Berg, Bartok, Ades, Glennie, et al appeared first on Sequenza21.
