items.body: Words by Justin TurfordIt’s bloody hard work trying to exist as a musician these days. Not ‘slave working in a coltan mine’ hard but tricky enough to navigate a world that has decided that music (and creativity in general) is something no longer worth paying the creator for. One musician who has regularly and bravely shared his own struggles about life in the independent music business is South Londoner Adam Scrimshire who if you don’t yet know then you should. A co-founder of the label Wah Wah 45s and now the one-man label head of Albert’s Favourites, an excellent record label dedicated to his own releases and a swathe of artists united by an emotional sensitivity and love for the deeper end of the groove pool, he is an underappreciated talent and a fine example of quiet determination.Over the years he has covered a lot of musical bases. From the soulful guest vocalist excursions of 2019’s ‘Listeners’ to the frustrated fury and free jazz-channeling collaborations with Idris Rahman, Nat Birchall and Tamar Osborne on 2021’s ‘Paroxysm’, Adam has proved adept at creating real music with real heart and emotion. The sheer number of top class collaborators who have been attracted to his orbit reveals an artist and producer of great taste and empathy. A successful collaboration takes more than an invitation to succeed.Here, on his ninth album, Adam has pushed through and overcome his doubts once again to deliver, in my opinion, his masterpiece. Five years in the making,  'Bring Our Light To Every Corner' contains six beautiful compositions of reflective soul, spiritual jazz and pastoral folk, awash with love and a much needed sense of unhurried time. Despite clearly drawing on the musical language of the late 60s and 70s psyche-soul-jazz-folk crossover period, the album never feels like he is trying to recreate an aesthetic. Without sounding like them directly, the record shares the DNA of 70s artists such as Stepney-era Terry Callier, Nick Drake and Pentangle, songwriters who understood the inherent romance of nature and how small stories reveal larger truths. We could also throw into the mix the widescreen sonic cinema of Arthur Verocai, Isaac Hayes or the Siberian musical traveller Misha Sultan: musician-arrangers with a knack for knowing when to keep it simple and when to go fully baroque.  “I wanted to create somewhere people could stay for a while.. A space that carries you gently through the record.”Space is certainly the place on the David Axelrod-channelling album starter, ‘My Land Is Your Land, Your Sky Is My Sky’. Chris Boot’s measured drums sit tight and loud over a slow-moving groove of tremolo guitar, sustained keys, Mark Zentai’s electric sitar and a brooding bass and piano riff that DJ Shadow could only dream about. Soprano saxophonist Jake Telford brings a searching, ecstatic energy as the song lifts from the Earth.The legendary Los Angeles jazz singer Dwight Trible brings his wordless Leon Thomas-like voicing to the cosmic hallucination of ‘Asleep, A Dream’. Also joined by harpist Amanda Whiting and Idris Rahman on flute and saxophone, Adam has created a timeless slice of funky, spiritual soul jazz with afrobeat-esque drums, huge strings and cheeky clavinet and Moog twiddling to add to the fun. A piece of music that makes me want to smile deeply.The title track ‘Bring Our Light To Every Corner’ is a handclapping communal singalong with a choir comprised of Rob Hynd, Daudi Matsiko, Jay Brown and Faye Houston joining Adam in a warming embrace of “La La La’s” over a delicate acoustic guitar, congas, hand percussion and vintage synths (all played by Adam). Churchy but earthy, it sits somewhere between Alice Coltrane’s funky mantras on her 1977 LP ‘Transcendence’ and the more pared back tracks of Leeds’ Ancient Infinity Orchestra. Needless to say, I love this vibe.The ever-brilliant keys maestro Jessica Lauren locks down her piano chops on the jazz-gospel-Northern soul bumper ‘With Our Eternal Hope And Joy’. Joined again by a (slightly different) choir and Idris Rahman on flute and sax, the song pulsates with the hope and joyfulness of its title. The main melodic hook is a beauty and when Joshu Idehen steps in to add some words of positive power before the late surge of full band energy, I can only wish that I had been in that room.‘Your Heart Is My Heart, My Hand Is Your Hand’ is an incredibly beautiful piece of meditative music. Adam plays his Rhodes with a subdued grace as Indian classical vocalist Mahesh Kale delicately invokes Shanti whilst shivers of strings and Jake Telford’s soprano saxophone electrifies the air. The album is only six songs strong but its concluding composition more than makes up for it. ‘Awake, A Dream’ is a spectacular epic made up of three distinct movements and comes in just shy of fifteen minutes long. The first third is a symphonic dream of pastoral bliss with acoustic guitar, piano and sweeping strings, long-time collaborator Faye Houston’s soulful harmonic voicing adding a woozy romance to this section. Silence. Chris Boot’s tight breakbeat and Adam’s picked bass enter the stage as Rhodes, acoustic guitar and stacked layers of Faye’s celestial voice unfurl and fill the atmosphere. The groove inhales and exhales for just the right amount of time before falling into a slumbering piano line, inviting Faye to step to the front. “Everything that we, everything that we dream” she sings with increasing urgency, high sustained strings and her own rich backing vocals shimmering like vibrations on water. Adam thinks this may be his favourite piece of music he’s made to date and I’m not surprised. It’s quite magnificent.There is a lot of great music being released this year but I suspect when I’ve forgotten some of those records (as you do), ‘Bring Our Light To Every Corner’ will be remembered as one of the best albums of 2026. 10/10.BUY HERE! https://scrimshire.bandcamp.com/album/bring-our-light-to-every-corner

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Scrimshire在独立音乐领域坚持多年的沉淀之作，耗时五年完成，收录六首融合灵魂乐、精神爵士与田园民谣的作品。乐评指出，专辑虽明显借鉴60年代末至70年代的迷幻灵魂爵士与民谣交叉时期的语言，但并非复古模仿，而是与Terry Callier、Nick Drake等艺术家的精神脉络相通。制作上强调空间感与缓慢流动的时间，开场曲以沉稳鼓组、颤音吉他、电西塔琴和低音钢琴构建出深邃律动，萨克斯与爵士歌手的即兴吟唱带来升腾感。专辑邀请多位合作者参与，体现了创作者在编曲上的克制与宏大之间的平衡，整体氛围温暖、内省，适合沉浸式聆听。

items.body: Zwickau’s Elektrisch Festival returns on 24 October 2026 with a line-up that makes a convincing argument for electronic music as a continuum rather than a museum of separate generations. At one end stands Portion Control, active since 1979 and fundamental to the development of British industrial electronics; around them are Hungarian EBM veterans Escalator, the much newer KRIEG-B, and the contemporary projects OSZYLAYTER and Cyborg Projekt X. The 19th Elektrisch Festival takes place at Club Seilerstraße, Seilerstraße 1B, 08056 Zwickau. Doors open at 19:00, with the programme beginning at 20:00. The final line-up announced by organiser emmobiz Records is Portion Control, Escalator, OSZYLAYTER, Cyborg Projekt X and KRIEG-B. A festival with a rather unusual history Elektrisch is not a newly invented festival carrying an impressive number. Its history reaches back well before the current revival. Contemporary reports document the 11th edition in 2007, the 12th in 2008, the 13th in 2009, and two editions, numbers 14 and 15, in 2010, then held at Zwickau’s BPM Club. Artists appearing during that period included names such as Absolute Body Control, Birmingham 6, Tyske Ludder and The Klinik. Then Elektrisch disappeared for fourteen years. emmobiz Records revived it in 2024 with the 16th Elektrisch Festival, now at Club Seilerstraße. That return was already sold out months in advance and brought together Calva Y Nada, Cat Rapes Dog, Digital Factor and Accessory. The 17th edition followed in October 2025 with Test Dept, NZ, In Strict Confidence, Supreme Court and To Avoid. In February 2026, the 18th Elektrisch expanded across two evenings, separating a synthpop-oriented first night from a harder EBM/electro programme on the second. That history makes the 2026 autumn line-up apt: Elektrisch has repeatedly connected artists from different phases of underground electronic music instead of reducing EBM to one historical period. Portion Control The obvious historical heavyweight is Portion Control. Formed in London in 1979, the group emerged from the early British industrial-electronic underground and became important for its use of synthesisers, drum machines and sampling long before those methods became standard practice. Their influence has subsequently been acknowledged in connection with artists including Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly, Nine Inch Nails, Orbital and Nitzer Ebb; they also toured with Depeche Mode in 1984. But calling Portion Control a heritage act would miss what remains interesting about them. They returned in the 2000s and have continued producing new work rather than maintaining the early catalogue. This August they released “1983-86 – Hit The Pulse to Purge…”, their first major Artoffact archival box, while their official site simultaneously continues to define the project rather succinctly as “uncompromising dark electronic audio.” Zwickau is currently one of only two forthcoming live appearances listed on their Bandcamp. Escalator Escalator brings another kind of history to the evening. The Hungarian project was founded in Budapest in 1988 by 2RT+TB and belongs to the late-’80s/early-’90s generation of European Electronic Body Music. Its musical roots lie in the harder intersection of EBM and industrial electronics, with early influences including Kraftwerk, Throbbing Gristle, Cabaret Voltaire, Clock DVA and Front 242. Escalator’s history has been anything but linear; long gaps between releases and activity have been part of the project, yet its work has remained closely associated with the physical, stripped-back mechanics of classic body music. Their presence next to Portion Control is more than an “old-school” pairing: the two acts come from different geographical and chronological points in the development of electronic body music. OSZYLAYTER The German OSZYLAYTER represents a much more recent strand of the line-up. Public biographical information on the project is relatively sparse, so it is better not to manufacture a grand history that isn’t there. What can be verified is a growing Bandcamp catalogue including “Hate This Day”, “Lover Boy”, “Free Girls” and “Dig It in the Dirt”, while current Elektrisch coverage places the project on the modern dark-electro/industrial side of the bill. In the context of Elektrisch, that relative newness is actually useful. This isn’t five bands demonstrating variations of exactly the same established EBM formula; OSZYLAYTER helps shift the evening toward newer club electronics and shows where some of those older physical principles have travelled. Cyborg Projekt X Cyborg Projekt X is similarly one of the less extensively documented names on the programme. The confirmed festival announcement places the project alongside OSZYLAYTER as part of the contemporary dark-electro and industrial side of the line-up, with an emphasis on forceful, club-oriented electronics. That makes Cyborg Projekt X something of the unknown variable of the evening, especially for listeners arriving primarily for the established EBM names. In a festival whose history has always mixed recognised acts with smaller projects, that is hardly out of character. KRIEG-B KRIEG-B is much newer as a project but comes with considerable history behind its members. The duo was formed in June 2023 by Dominique Lallement, known from Kriegbereit, Cobalt 60 and K-Bereit, and Benoît Buyse, associated with Dreadfool, Anamorphosis and Nihiliste. The project describes its music as a meeting point between industrial electronics, EBM and darkwave, drawing on several decades of electronic music rather than one specific period. Their debut album “War Drums’ Resonance” arrived in November 2024, with tracks including “S.C.S.N”, “Parabellum”, “Artificial Minds”, “Truth Lies” and “King of Emptiness”. In a sense, KRIEG-B makes a neat closing piece to the Elektrisch concept: a young project constructed by musicians carrying several earlier generations of European industrial electronics with them. More than the line-up The revived Elektrisch has also developed a strong physical-release component. The 18th edition was accompanied by exclusive 10-inch festival vinyl releases, while emmobiz has already announced a V.A. “19. Elektrisch Festival” 10-inch connected to this year’s event. The appeal of the 19th edition goes beyond Portion Control finally returning to Zwickau. The five acts represent very different positions within the same broad history: British industrial experimentation, Hungarian old-school EBM, contemporary German dark electronics, and a new Franco-Belgian project carrying the experience of earlier industrial formations into something current. That is probably the strongest reason to pay attention to Elektrisch. After a fourteen-year absence, the festival did not return simply to recreate the period in which it originally existed. Its current identity depends on putting that history into the same room with what came after it. 19. Elektrisch Festival: date, venue and line-up Elektrisch Festival 24 October 2026 Club Seilerstraße Seilerstraße 1B, 08056 Zwickau, Germany Line-up: Portion Control Escalator OSZYLAYTER Cyborg Projekt X KRIEG-B Doors: 19:00 Start: 20:00 Tickets are available through emmobiz Records.
items._cn_summary: 该报道介绍第19届Elektrisch音乐节的阵容与历史，强调其作为电子音乐连续体的定位。演出包括英国工业电子先驱Portion Control、匈牙利EBM老将Escalator、新锐KRIEG-B以及当代项目OSZYLAYTER和Cyborg Projekt X。音乐节自2007年起在德国茨维考举办，曾中断十四年，2024年由独立厂牌emmobiz Records恢复。报道特别指出Portion Control自1979年活跃至今，其早期合成器与采样手法影响深远，且仍在持续创作。音乐节通过邀请不同年代的艺人，将工业、EBM与新兴电子场景串联，而非将其固化为历史遗产。活动于2026年10月24日在Club Seilerstraße举行，19时开门，20时演出开始。

items.body: Corlyx released “Your Heart In The Serpent’s Mouth” on August 20, 2026 through Out Of Line Music. The track runs 4:08 and slows the tempo of the guitar-led singles the band have issued through 2026, moving their gothic rock toward dream pop textures. It is the third single of the year, and the digital release bundles it with the two that came before it: “More Anarchy” and “Sweeter Than Blood”, three tracks across 10:47. Caitlin Stokes wrote the lyrics and melody, and produced and arranged the track with Brandon Ashley, who wrote and performed the guitars. Davide Rocco played bass and Flow Toulman wrote and performed the drums. Ashley mixed and mastered the single at Dtuned Brighton Productions. Stokes describes the single as part of a wider look at the era the band draw from rather than a change of direction. “We are exploring all the beautiful colours of this time period,” she stated. “Gothic Rock is at the core but so much was going around the subculture at this time, and currently there isn’t a lot of representation for rock genres in the scene – one of the many advantages of having a full band line up now is to explore these sounds.” She named a long-standing interest in Cocteau Twins as the reference point for the track, called it “quite experimental even for us”, and said the band hesitated over releasing a slower song as a single at all – “but really anything goes at this point and I love it so much.” Ashley built the guitar sound to that brief. “Lets make the guitars super dreamy for this track, was a request by Caitlin and I obliged,” he stated. “I have my own unique tones that I spent a very long time creating, so we don’t necessarily sound like Cocteau Twins, but they were certainly an inspiration for this track.” Stokes gives the lyric two readings. “Your heart in the serpents mouth, fragile and delicate, always in danger of being eaten alive, or worse,” she explained. “It’s a tale of trust and vulnerability, accepting the fates of love and the fears that come with this.” Your Heart In The Serpent’s Mouth by Corlyx The 2026 run began with “Sweeter Than Blood” on May 28, followed by “More Anarchy” on July 9, the more directly political of the three and the only one so far with an accompanying music video. Out Of Line has scheduled a Corlyx album for early 2027; no title or date has been announced. The single is on Bandcamp and the usual streaming services, and Out Of Line has published an official audio version on its own YouTube channel. About Corlyx Corlyx are the project of singer and songwriter Caitlin Stokes and guitarist and producer Brandon Ashley, originally from Los Angeles and now based in Brighton, with Out Of Line describing the group as living between the UK and Italy. The duo self-released the EP “One Of Us” on February 13, 2016, then the albums “Music 2 F 2” on February 3, 2018 and “In2 The Skin” on August 16, 2019. They joined the Negative Gain Productions roster in September 2020 with “Together Apart”. The move to Out Of Line Music followed with the “Raindrops” EP on March 31, 2022, and Side-Line covered the video for the “Raindrops” single that March. The single “Never Love” arrived on October 5, 2022 and the album “Blood In The Disco” on November 25, 2022, trailed by the single and video for “Take Off Everything” the previous December. The double album “Purple Pain”, nineteen tracks, followed on February 14, 2025, after the band announced it alongside the single “Zombie Kid” in November 2024. Collaboration has run through the catalogue. Stokes sang on ESA‘s “Eat Their Young” video and EP in 2020; Suzi Sabotage featured on the 2023 single “Kill Cave”; and the band appeared on Meersein‘s “Her Slave” the same year. On Out Of Line the band share a roster with Till Lindemann and Aesthetic Perfection. The addition of Rocco on bass and Toulman on drums has taken Corlyx from a studio-centred duo to a full band, which is the change Stokes points to when explaining where “Your Heart In The Serpent’s Mouth” came from.
items._cn_summary: 乐队于2026年8月20日通过独立厂牌发行第三支单曲，时长4分08秒。作品将此前吉他主导的哥特摇滚节奏放缓，转向梦幻流行质感的声响。主唱负责词曲与制作，并与吉他手共同完成编曲；吉他音色被刻意处理得迷离朦胧。主唱称创作以极地双子星为参照，意在探索哥特摇滚亚文化周边时代的声音色彩，并形容这支单曲“对我们来说也相当实验”。歌词围绕“心在蛇口中”的意象展开，讨论信任与脆弱。数字版还收录了该年早前发行的两支单曲。

items.album: Godflesh set penultimate album ‘Decay’ for 25 September on Relapse

items.body: The six tracks on “Decay” came out of the same sessions as “Purge” three years ago, and Justin Broadrick held them back while he looked for a label. He found one: the tenth Godflesh album arrives on 25 September 2026 through Relapse Records, the first the Birmingham industrial duo have issued outside Broadrick’s own Avalanche Recordings since their 2010 return. “Living/Ending” is the first single. “Decay” is the penultimate Godflesh album, not the last one. Broadrick has said a further record is written and still to be recorded, and in March 2026 he announced the end of Godflesh live performances after abdominal surgery for a hernia. Broadrick explained where the record came from and why it took three years to surface: “Decay was born from the same sessions as Purge,” he stated. “It was one huge pool of songs. I picked what I felt was appropriate for what I wanted to achieve with Purge, with the intention of releasing the songs that didn’t fit as a new album within a year of Purge being released. Unfortunately, two years passed whilst considering external labels, so that I didn’t have to self-release GODFLESH anymore, but it took an awful lot of time to establish a comfortable home for me. The recordings were done, but as usual for me, I did change a lot of stuff once I came back to it.” The band have done this before. “Decline & Fall”, issued on 2 June 2014, was built the same way, from tracks Broadrick cut from the sessions that produced “A World Lit Only By Fire” four months later. He also addressed how the surgery intersected with the recording, since the hernia itself came from the way he sings: “Fortunately, all of the recordings for Decay were completed long before the surgery, vocals included… although the back end of a couple of songs were recorded with the hernia itself, and that was a struggle. I was already aware that the GODFLESH shout, so to speak, was exacerbating the hernia greatly, as was every GODFLESH performance in the lead-up to the surgery once the hernia appeared, and the hernia was mostly caused by year upon year of shouting in GODFLESH. The album was mixed post-surgery, and while I was still in some pain and considerable discomfort, but fortunately GODFLESH is generally me expressing my pain, albeit [usually] mental, philosophical and existential, whereas this was physical pain.” Broadrick points to the opening and closing tracks as the record’s core, and notes that the two of them together run half its length: “The bookends of Decay are the most important pieces to me. They say it all, so to speak; the album could have been just those two songs alone – the duration of them is half of the total album!” Decay by GODFLESH Godflesh ‘Decay’ tracklist and formats The album runs six tracks: “Master and Slave” “Living/Ending” “Feral Colony” “Fear Of Man” “Fodder” “Consume Me” Relapse Records offers “Decay” on 12-inch vinyl, CD and cassette, with a digital edition through Bandcamp. A deluxe 12-inch pressing in two limited colours, housed in a silver board laminated jacket with gloss UV and packaged with a slipmat, poster and sticker, has already sold out at the label store. About Godflesh Justin Broadrick and bassist G.C. Green formed Godflesh in Birmingham, England, in 1988. Broadrick had played guitar on side one of Napalm Death’s “Scum” the year before, and the pair built Godflesh around downtuned guitar, bass and a drum machine rather than a live drummer. The self-titled debut EP arrived in 1988, followed by the album “Streetcleaner” on Earache Records on 13 November 1989. “Pure” came in 1992. The band ran until 2002, when Broadrick ended the project during a US tour; “Hymns”, from 2001, was the last album of that period. He spent the following years on Jesu and other projects before reactivating Godflesh in 2010 with Green. The reunion output came out on Broadrick’s own Avalanche Recordings. The “Decline & Fall” EP appeared on 2 June 2014 and the seventh album, “A World Lit Only By Fire”, on 7 October 2014. “Post Self” followed in October 2017 on vinyl and CD. Six years later the duo returned with the ninth album “Purge” on 9 June 2023, previewed by “the ‘Nero’ single and a US tour announcement”. Away from Godflesh, Broadrick records as JK Flesh and has remixed and contributed to work by acts including Pitchshifter and Derision Cult, the latter alongside members of Ministry and The Cure. “Decay” leaves one Godflesh album still to record. On what closing the project means, Broadrick stated: “It expresses my pain, and I’ve put my body and soul into this expression for the majority of my existence. I feel quite lucky, because Godflesh is now physically impossible for me, rendering it useless. I now wish to move out of its constraints, move on creatively with heavy/ugly music to new ground.”
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是英国双人组的第十张录音室专辑，也是乐队宣布的倒数第二张专辑。它与三年前的前作出自同一批创作素材，核心人物贾斯汀·布罗德里克从大量曲目中挑选后重新加工，并耗时两年寻找外部厂牌，最终由独立厂牌发行。专辑共六首曲目，首尾两首长度合计占全辑一半，布罗德里克称这两首是核心。人声与器乐录制在疝气手术前完成，部分曲目末尾在带伤状态下录制，混音则于术后进行。这张专辑延续了乐队标志性的沉重声响，同时因身体状况而带出更直接的身体疼痛维度。

items.body: I’m lost in this sea of lies And every voice is pulling me The deeper that I sink below The harder it becomes to breathe A society driven by private desires gradually leads people to confuse exploitation with intelligence. Deception becomes a normal part of life, loyalty is conditional, and every interaction is seen as a strategic move for personal gain. For those still seeking genuine sincerity, this creates a strange sense of suffocation, as if each compromise raises the water level a little higher. “Drowning,” the newest single by Leipzig’s Kalte Steine, explores the psychological cost of moving through a culture increasingly shaped by self-interest, duplicity, and the pursuit of personal advantage at any cost. Continuing the English-language direction introduced on “Crying Out,” the track translates that social exhaustion into the sensation of sinking through an immeasurable body of water. The song opens with waves sighing against the shore before a bass line and drum machine enter, beating with the strained regularity of a heart short on oxygen. A quivering keyboard accent appears beside a simple melodic post-punk guitar figure, leaving broad spaces inside the arrangement. The economy of the playing and the grave tonal balance recall Pink Turns Blue at their starkest. The vocals drift in through delay and reverb, soft and mournful, with a natural English cadence settling easily across the meter. Their restraint suits the song’s depleted state, allowing “I’m drowning” to fall with the blunt force of an admission repeated too many times. The delivery stays low and controlled, placing fatigue at its expressive center. The lyrics recast dishonesty as an ocean without a visible boundary. Every voice pulls the singer deeper, the vanished shore removes any point of return, and the rising tide turns gradual ethical decay into a daily physical threat. “Lost in this sea of lies” describes both the surrounding culture and the point at which prolonged exposure to it has entered the body. Around the one-minute mark, the arrangement opens for the arrival of buzzing retro synthesizers, while the guitar flutters overhead like gulls crossing the waves. “The harder it becomes to breathe” is repeated, with the second delivery reduced to a whisper. Later, the same whispered echo follows “I’ve been drowning here for years,” changing a direct declaration into something barely confessed. In that sense, “Drowning” examines the exhaustion of preserving one’s humanity in a system that rewards manipulation. The plea to be taken beyond fear and washed clean of tears carries a desire for moral as well as physical escape. Years of submersion have left the song’s protagonist too tired to fight the tide, yet the act of identifying the water as a “sea of lies” preserves a final measure of clarity. “Drowning” is Kalte Steine’s most accomplished release so far. The songwriting holds its central metaphor from the first line to the last, the production grants each instrument greater definition, and the vocal performance gains authority through control. Those advances make its desolation more immediate, bringing sharper emotional and musical focus to the project’s familiar grey terrain. Listen to “Drowning” below: Kalte Steine’s previous singles—“Shattered,” “Dysthymia,” “Wüste aus Beton,” “Kinder der Nacht,” and “Crying Out”—established a monochrome world of private fracture, civic numbness, and nocturnal escape. As explored in our earlier feature on the project, those songs allowed inner conflict and a cold, dystopian exterior to blur into one another. “Drowning” is out now on all major streaming platforms. Follow Kalte Steine: Instagram Spotify SoundCloud TikTok The post “I’m Lost in This Sea of Lies” — Leipzig Darkwave Project Kalte Steine is Caught in a Deluge of Duplicity in “Drowning” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: 莱比锡乐队Kalte Steine的新单曲《Drowning》延续了上一首英文作品的路线，以溺水隐喻当代社会中因普遍虚伪与自利而生的窒息感。歌曲以海浪声开场，贝斯与鼓机营造出缺氧般的心跳节奏，吉他与合成器保持克制留白，人声在延迟与混响中低沉漂浮，疲惫感成为情感核心。歌词将谎言比作无边海洋，反复出现的“我在溺水”在耳语式重复中从宣言变为近乎自白的脆弱。整体编曲简洁，氛围阴暗，与Pink Turns Blue早期风格相近，是乐队迄今对核心意象执行最完整的一次创作。

items.body: “Vaga” came out of a London heatwave: a baião rhythm from Northeast Brazil, a maracatu-inspired groove, and a lift that recalls Sérgio Mendes. Lead vocalist Claudia Marques sings over a core of drums and keys, framing love as a boundless, constant current meant for everyone, with a roots-style female chorus behind her and flute lines over the top. Flautist Rachel Hayter weaves melodic lines alongside a backing chorus featuring Inês Loubet and Ana De Llor. Guitarist Jackson Caines, bassist Giovanni Cresseri, and drummer Jonny Venvell guide the arrangement into an energetic breakdown before tipping into a final key change. It is the first single from Novos Londrinos, a five-piece based in North London whose name nods to Novos Baianos, the Brazilian group from the 1970s, and reads as “new Londoners”. The players met in 2021 in a samba bateria, Rhythms of the City, then kept going through house jams, pulled together by 60s and 70s Brazilian music: the songwriting of Marcos Valle, the voice of Elis Regina. Their self-titled debut EP, recorded at Giant Wafer and Abbey Road Studios, reaches past bossa nova and samba into baião, spiritual jazz and Cape Verdean rhythms. Across it, Claudia Marques writes between lightness and introspection, turning over new arrivals, the passing of time, and the beautiful and unfamiliar. They played Glastonbury in 2025 and shared a Porto stage with Ivan Lins‘s bassist. On 22 November, they take a London Jazz Festival slot at Milton Court. Stream “Vaga” and get your copy of their debut EP HERE The post Daily Discovery: Novos Londrinos – Vaga appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body:
Siiry Debuts As A Producer With Fuzzy Melancholic Dance Pop Single 'Deja Vu'

20 August 2026

After rising as a DJ through this decade, Hyderabad's Siiry assumes the role of a producer with her debut single 'Deja Vu'.

Though packing a bouncy groove that gets the body moving like her efforts on the dancefloor, Siiry chooses an entirely different aim with the track as she creates "an ode to nostalgia — a love letter to everything that feels familiar and comfortable, including the patterns - both good and bad - that we find ourselves returning to."

Consequently, the song comes with the fuzzy textures and detuned keys that evoke that melancholic yearning-for-past feeling very dominantly found in lo-fi house, except delivered over a more dynamic interplay of drums and bass. Alongside the synth interludes, Siiry buries her voice in echoey washes till it just about switches from being the central songwriting to an ambient layer. All of it serves a single emotional purpose, and that in itself showcases surprising musical maturity, especially for a debut production.

Watch the music video for 'Deja Vu' below and follow Siiry for more information.

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由洛杉矶乐队Los Cenzontles发起，以墨西哥与夏威夷之间的历史迁徙为线索，串联起两种看似遥远却共享牛仔传统的音乐文化。作品涵盖西班牙语、夏威夷语与英语的歌曲，包括老歌新唱、新创作及传统美国民谣，编曲上以尤克里里、吉他、墨西哥竖琴和手风琴形成密集而统一的织体。Taj Mahal与David Hidalgo的参与带来深厚音乐底蕴，Sonny Lim的滑棒吉他与松弛弦独奏增添了即兴色彩。录音在五天内以同室现场方式完成，保留了自然的互动与即兴空间，学生与资深乐手同场合作，体现了跨代际、跨文化的协作精神。对伍迪·格思里《Deportee》的演绎也赋予移民议题现实关怀，使整张专辑兼具历史纵深与当代意义。

The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Dominique Cravic与Robert Crumb共同构想，以复古78转唱片为素材，用手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门、夏威夷吉他、乐锯等杂糅乐器重新演绎。音乐融合了巴尔-缪赛特、拉格泰姆、jug band、法国香颂与skiffle等风格，既保留老唱片的怀旧质感，又因古怪的配器和即兴式的编排而显得鲜活。27首短曲大多由Cravic以近似Maurice Chevalier的说唱方式演绎，手风琴贯穿其中。曲目涵盖幽默的《Ukulele Lady》和致敬法国抵抗运动歌手Juliette Gréco的严肃作品，也翻玩了《Smoke Gets in Your Eyes》《Take Five》《As Time Goes By》等经典旋律。乐评认为这是一部充满好奇心与严肃态度的作品，让被遗忘的音乐重新焕发生机，类似Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks的难以归类气质。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的出道EP，数字发行，共五首曲目，以传统北欧民谣为基底，由主唱Mia Guldhammer领衔。乐队为多数传统曲目带来个人视角，整体弥漫古老而略带粗粝的氛围。开篇《Svennedal》以起伏的节奏展现歌者富有说服力的嗓音；《Nordgård》是唯一原创曲目，口弦与风笛带来持续推动力。传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》中钦巴龙琴构成细腻底色，口弦与其它乐器交织；结尾器乐曲《Ormsö》以口弦、长笛和弦乐营造出灵动且偏离常规的声响。五首作品显示出乐队已相当成熟，是一张有分量的开端。

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑由MoE与鼓手Ikuro Takahashi及萨克斯手Signe Emmeluth合作录制于挪威Børsen文化空间。MoE的核心成员是吉他手Håvard Skaset与贝斯手兼主唱Guro S. Moe，他们的音乐横跨朋克、噪音与即兴领域，追求高强度与大音量，不依附于任何固定流派。专辑以现场形式呈现，捕捉了乐手之间的即兴碰撞与能量爆发，融合了粗粝的吉他噪音、低频贝斯线条与自由爵士的呼吸感。三位不同背景的音乐人在舞台上形成对话，将噪音摇滚的冲击力与即兴演奏的不可预测性结合在一起，体现出地下实验场景中跨地域合作的可能性。

The record draws on Davachi’s many years of engagement with historical instruments and fascination with various tuning systems, textures and harmonic structures, featuring reconstructed period wind instruments, historically tuned organs and an abstracted Renaissance choral form. It also makes excellent use of the centuries of combined musical experience brought to bear by her many collaborators, most of whom are noted performer-composers themselves (Whitney Johnson, Eyvind Kang, and Lucy Railton among them). And then there’s the two-hour-plus runtime. Taken... The post Sarah Davachi – The Will of Tongues appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 萨拉·达瓦奇作为演奏家兼作曲家，多年来专注于历史乐器与各种调律体系的研究。本专辑是她多年探索的集大成之作，作品以管风琴为核心，辅以历史管乐器与抽象化的文艺复兴合唱形式。合作者多为同样具备深厚创作经验的演奏家与作曲家，丰富的演奏积累为作品提供了扎实的诠释基础。整张专辑时长超过两小时，结构宏大，强调深度聆听体验。文本涉及调律系统、音色纹理、和声结构的精细雕琢，呈现出跨越多个世纪的乐器与音乐传统的融合。这张专辑适合对历史乐器、当代古典与慢速冥想式聆听有耐心的听众。

items.body: Made in secret in the shadow of Soviet Normalization, after decades as a cult object Maťkovia's debut album has been newly reissued and expanded. Jakub Knera tells the extraordinary story of the project's leader Martin Burlas ‘Normalization’ in Czechoslovakia in the 1970s and 1980s was paradoxical: rather than a return to normality, it in fact meant renewed state control over society, culture, and public life. It followed the Prague Spring of 1968, which had grown out of the political and cultural relaxation of the 1960s, where under Alexander Dubček, reforms aimed to create ‘socialism with a human face’ allowed greater freedom of expression and artistic experimentation. The Soviet Union considered these reforms too radical, however, and in August 1968 Warsaw Pact... The post Reissue of the Week: Maťkovia’s 1982 – 1986 (Expanded) appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑诞生于捷克社会主义正常化时期的秘密创作环境，是东欧地下音乐的罕见实物。Maťkovia 由 Martin Burlas 领导，其首张专辑原为1982年发行的地下作品，此次再版进行了内容扩充。马丁·布尔拉斯的创作背景尤为特殊：作品在国家文化管制最严苛的时期秘密完成，反映了七十至八十年代捷克斯洛伐克地下艺术家在极有限空间内进行独立表达的处境。再版发行使这一长期仅在小范围内流传的文化档案进入更多听众视野，为研究东欧前卫摇滚与实验音乐脉络提供了重要素材。文章作为乐评信息有限，主要聚焦于历史语境而非音乐本体分析。

items.body: Dutch new wave duo Pol released the official video for “Sex Machines” on 21 August 2026. Fashion photographer and filmmaker Rémi Lamandé directed it. The single itself came out on 25 June 2026 as a two-track digital release on Bandcamp, pairing the 3:59 vocal version with an instrumental of the same length, and is also on streaming platforms. Pol are the brothers Ruben and Matthijs Pol, who are based in Paris. They gave “Sex Machines” a single launch show during Paris Fashion Week in June 2026, two months before the video appeared. How Pol built the ‘Sex Machines’ video Lamandé built the clip as a street interview programme. Ruben Pol carries a star-marked microphone through a service alley and holds it out to a series of passers-by, each of whom lip-syncs the lyric instead of answering. The cast then moves into a concrete parking garage, and the closing section shows the duo performing to a packed room under hard white backlight. A final outtake shows the two brothers laughing. The duo explained where the concept started: “It started off with the idea of doing an interview style video with a diverse cast of characters. We liked the idea of ‘strangers’ singing the song, similarly how the two ex-lovers in the lyrics are acting like strangers. We shared the idea with director Remi Lamandé who brought the full script to life.” The brothers wrote and produced the track themselves. Matthijs Pol plays drum computer, electric guitar, synths, xylophone and sings; Ruben Pol plays drum computer, electric guitar, synths, bass, vocoder and sings. Matthijs and Ruben mixed it with Paul D. Millar, and Gianni Peri mastered it. On their own Bandcamp page the duo describe the song as built on “twitching beats, serrated guitars and clipped vocals”. Sex Machines by Pol About Pol Pol is a duo formed by the Dutch brothers Ruben and Matthijs Pol, now based in Paris, France. Both play guitar, synthesizers and drum computer and both sing; Ruben adds bass and vocoder, Matthijs adds xylophone. The pair write, produce and mix their own recordings and handle their visuals, videos, merchandise and fanzines themselves. The brothers issued a self-titled debut EP in 2023. Two singles followed on their own Bandcamp: “Masks” in June 2024 and “The Chameleon” in December 2024. Their first zine, which documents a Western European tour, is stocked by the Paris bookshop Librairie 1909, and the same multidisciplinary practice has produced sound-design work for Louis Vuitton and Miu Miu. In 2024 the duo played their first headline show at a sold-out Bitterzoet in Amsterdam with Logan Sky of Visage, and have since performed in Europe, the United States and Japan. In early 2026 they opened sold-out Lebanon Hanover shows in London, Lille and Paris. “Sex Machines”, released on 25 June 2026, is their first new music since “The Chameleon”. The Rémi Lamandé video, out on 21 August 2026, is the first visual the duo have released from it.
items._cn_summary: 荷兰兄弟双人组Pol在巴黎发布了单曲《Sex Machines》的官方MV，由时尚摄影师兼导演Rémi Lamandé执导。MV以街头采访形式为概念，主唱Rubeno手持星形话筒在巷弄中随机采访路人，每位受访者以对口型方式回应歌词，呼应歌曲中两位前任恋人如陌生人般的疏离感，随后场景转入混凝土停车场，最终以白色强光下的现场演出收尾。歌曲由兄弟二人独立创作与制作，Matthijs负责鼓机、电吉他、合成器、木琴与人声，Ruben则加入贝斯与声码器，作品以抽搐式节拍、锯齿状吉他与碎片化人声为特征。作为一支涉猎音乐、视觉、出版物与时尚设计的跨领域组合，Pol曾为Louis Vuitton与Miu Miu提供声音设计，并活跃于欧洲、美国与日本巡演。整体风格偏向合成器驱动的暗色调新浪潮，介于后朋克与电子舞曲之间，具备一定的独立审美与DIY精神。

items.body: Leipzig darkwave project Kalte Steine released “Drowning” on 20 August 2026 as a self-released digital single. The track runs 4:39 and is available on Bandcamp and on streaming services. It is the project’s sixth single and the second sung entirely in English, following “Crying Out” from June 2026. Kalte Steine mix darkwave and post-punk: drum machine, bass, a spare guitar figure and vocals set well back in delay and reverb. On “Drowning” a field recording of waves opens the track before the rhythm section enters, and buzzing analogue synthesizers arrive about a minute in. Drowning by Kalte Steine Where ‘Drowning’ sits in the Kalte Steine catalogue The project’s first four singles, “Shattered”, “Dysthymia”, “Wüste aus Beton” and “Kinder der Nacht”, were sung in German and appeared on Bandcamp in June 2026. “Crying Out”, issued on 29 June 2026, was the first Kalte Steine track written and sung in English. “Drowning” continues in that language. All six tracks are self-released. Kalte Steine has no label, no album and no Discogs entry, and sells its catalogue directly through Bandcamp at a per-track price. The digital track download is offered in MP3, FLAC and 24-bit/44.1 kHz formats. About Kalte Steine Kalte Steine is a darkwave and post-punk project based in Leipzig, Germany. The project releases under its own name without a label and has not published a lineup, so the number of people involved is not documented. Recording activity began in mid-2026. Four German-language singles, “Shattered”, “Dysthymia”, “Wüste aus Beton” and “Kinder der Nacht”, went up on Bandcamp in June 2026, tagged by the project as alternative, darkwave, goth, gothic and post-punk. Those tracks set out the recording approach the project has kept since: drum machine, bass, single-line guitar, synthesizer, and vocals treated with delay and reverb rather than pushed forward in the mix. “Crying Out” arrived on 29 June 2026 and switched the writing to English. “Drowning” followed on 20 August 2026 as the second English-language track and the sixth release overall. Both are available on Bandcamp and on streaming platforms, and no physical edition has been issued.
items._cn_summary: 来自莱比锡的暗潮项目 Kalte Steine 发布第六首单曲《Drowning》，也是第二首全英文作品。制作采用经典暗潮编制：鼓机、贝斯、单线吉他与人声，人声大量使用延迟与混响处理后置于混音深处，呈现出冰冷疏离的气质。开场引入海浪实地录音，约一分钟后嗡嗡作响的模拟合成器层叠进入，使氛围在四分三十九秒的篇幅中由空旷转向压迫。作品以自助形式在 Bandcamp 及流媒体平台发行，提供 MP3、FLAC 与 24-bit/44.1 kHz 三种数字格式，无厂牌、无专辑、无实体版本，延续了该项目自 2026 年中以来以单曲为单位独立发表的运作方式。整体制作在类型框架内工整克制，声音美学清晰，但未展现出显著的实验突破或跨界融合元素。

items.body: Xasthur release “Open to Misinterpretation” on October 2, 2026 through Prophecy Productions. The nine-track album continues the acoustic, neofolk-leaning form Scott Conner adopted in 2015, and comes on CD digisleeve, black vinyl and digital. The tracklist runs “Running From Silence”, “Put You Out Of Your Misery”, “Mantras Of Delusion”, “Impersonating The Impostors”, “Nothing In The Dark”, “Waste Of Eternity”, “Prisoner Of Your Past”, “Strategic Incompetence” and “Death Can Heal”. The title is Conner’s answer to a long-running problem with how the project is read. Prophecy Productions describes the record as “a deeper and more developed version of what Conner already does”, made by an artist who has stopped trying to make the music easier to reach and has instead kept refining it. The label notes that the songs went through Xasthur’s touring on both sides of the Atlantic before they were recorded, and that the production is cleaner than on the previous albums while still aiming for a live, organic take. Open to Misinterpretation by Xasthur Two tracks have gone out ahead of the album, both as visualizers on the label’s YouTube channel. “Put You Out Of Your Misery” came first in July 2026, followed by “Nothing in the Dark” in August. About Xasthur Xasthur is the solo project of Scott Conner, who also records under the name Malefic and started it in Alhambra, California in December 1995. For its first fifteen years it was a black metal project, and Conner built its catalogue through a long run of small labels and split releases before the albums “Subliminal Genocide” (2006), “Defective Epitaph” (2007) and “All Reflections Drained” (2009) appeared on Hydra Head Records. Southern Lord had reissued “Nocturnal Poisoning” as a remastered double LP in 2005, and Conner spent those years guesting with Sunn O))) and Twilight. Conner retired the Xasthur name in 2010 and spent five years recording as Nocturnal Poisoning, releasing “Other Worlds of the Mind” in 2012, “A Misleading Reality” in 2013 and “Doomgrass” in 2014. On March 5, 2015 he announced that Xasthur would return, but as an acoustic project rather than a black metal one. The first album in that form, “Subject to Change”, followed on May 6, 2016 through Disharmonic Variations. The Prophecy Productions run began with “Victims of the Times” in 2021 and continued with “Inevitably Dark” in 2023 and “Disharmonic Variations” in 2024, each also issued in a deluxe edition. Two archival split collections, “Vol. 1 Splits 2002-2004” and “Vol. 2 Splits & Bonus 2007-2009”, came out on Lupus Lounge in 2024, and the early album “A Gate Through Bloodstained Mirrors” was reissued on gatefold double vinyl in 2026. “Open to Misinterpretation” is the fourth Xasthur album for Prophecy, and the label notes that its songs were road-tested before they were recorded.
items._genre: neofolk / acoustic / dark ambient / post-black metal
items._cn_summary: Xasthur 的这张专辑延续了 Scott Conner 自 2015 年转型以来的原声民谣路线，标题本身即回应了外界对其音乐长期存在的误读问题。九首作品经过大西洋两岸的巡演打磨后录制，编曲更加干净，但保留了现场感和有机质地。Conner 不再试图让音乐变得更易接近，而是继续精炼其原有的美学。从早期的黑金属到转型后的原声作品，这张专辑被厂牌描述为对其既有风格的更深层次发展。Prophecy Productions 是个专注于黑暗和前卫音乐的独立厂牌，与该用户的暗潮和实验音乐口味有交集，但作品本身更偏向内敛的民谣表达，实验性元素有限。

items.body: Aggrotech and dark electro project Subliminal Code released “Behind the Mask” through Neon Retro Records on July 31, 2026, and expanded it on August 16 with a fifth track. The label edition carried four cuts; the version on the project’s own Bandcamp page adds a remix by Dominator. The full running order is the title track (4:35), a People Theatre remix (5:01), an Elektroterapi remix (2:48), a club version (4:35) and the Dominator remix (3:15). Raúl J. Padrón wrote, produced and sang it and drew the artwork; Raúl Jr. Padrón handled synths and programming; Vitor Mancini mixed and mastered. The source material is horror cinema, and the project says so plainly on the release page: “Inspired by the dark atmosphere of classic slasher horror films, Behind the Mask tells the story of an unstoppable killer lurking in the shadows, where every step could be your last. Cold synths, crushing beats, distorted vocals, and relentless aggression come together to create the soundtrack for your darkest nightmare.” Three of the four extra versions push the track further toward the dancefloor than the original does, moving it from aggrotech and dark electro toward industrial techno. The release is digital. Behind the Mask by Subliminal Code About Subliminal Code Subliminal Code was founded at the start of 2010 by Raúl José Padrón and Raúl Junior Padrón, drawing on EBM, industrial, metal and synthpop. The project began in Venezuela and is now based in Budapest, Hungary, where Raúl José Padrón carries it as the sole permanent member. The first release, the “Soldier Of Hell” EP, appeared on December 23, 2011 through Engraved Ritual, followed by the single “The Beautiful People” in 2013 and “Another Day” on March 24, 2014. The debut album “Karma In Mortem” arrived on July 14, 2014 on the Hungarian label Advoxya Records, which then issued “Karma In Covers” on November 1, 2016 – a set of covers of Venezuelan metal bands – and “Soldier Of Hell, Reborn” three days later. In 2016 the project also appeared on Insane Records’ compilation “Terror Night Vol.2 Sound Of Dead Future”. Side-Line covered the single “Malevolencia” when it appeared on February 29, 2020, trailing the second album. That album, “The Cancer Of The World Is Human Beings”, came out on May 1, 2021 on Advoxya with eleven tracks. Since then the project has worked mainly in singles and short releases: the seven-track “I Never” on September 1, 2022, “Push Me Down” that November, “Memento Mori” on October 10, 2023, “Your Wish” on July 20, 2024 and “Void Of Morgoth” on July 15, 2025. “Behind the Mask” is the first Subliminal Code release to carry Neon Retro Records, a synthwave netlabel running since July 2019, and the first to be built out as a remix package rather than a standalone track.

items._cn_summary: 本文是关于Subliminal Code单曲《Behind the Mask》及其remix版本的资讯型报道。文章详细列出了五个版本的曲目时长、幕后制作人员分工，并附有创作背景介绍。音乐灵感源自经典砍杀恐怖电影的黑暗氛围，以冷冽合成器、重型节奏、失真人声与持续攻击性构成整体听觉框架。四个额外版本中有三个将原始轨道从aggrotech与dark electro推向industrial techno方向。文中还梳理了项目自2010年成立以来从委内瑞拉到匈牙利的迁徙轨迹，历年发行脉络与厂牌合作历史，包括Advoxya Records与Neon Retro Records等独立厂牌的关联。文章属于信息性内容，未涉及深入的音乐批评或艺术性评价。

items.body: Freedom is not the same as improvement, because freedom concerns our relationship to what happens, not merely the circumstances themselves. A prison can be renovated and still remain a prison in the mind. When suffering has organized your habits, loyalties, and sense of self, its removal may feel strangely like a loss. Anger often outlives the conditions that produced it because the body keeps yesterday’s argument alive. So when life improves, there is no commandment that says gratitude must arrive immediately. Sometimes liberation begins with allowing the old anger to exhaust itself, until you discover you no longer need it. There is something peculiarly German about naming a post-punk record Kleinkunst, a word usually reserved for cabaret, small-stage performance, and other modest forms of cultural production, then filling it with the psychic debris of cities built for industries that have vanished. Mottek87 comes from Duisburg, where structural change is hardly an abstraction. Zbigniew F. and Jürgen W., longtime friends of Polish descent, formed the duo in 2024 after an evening of drinking beer and listening to records somehow turned into the decision to make one themselves. Their music has retained something of that unceremonious beginning: guitars, bass, programmed drums, sparse synthesizers, and German lyrics delivered with the plainspoken severity of people suspicious of excessive decoration. The three songs on Kleinkunst: the title track, Oszillation, and Widerstand, concern a particular kind of estrangement, in which a person remains in the same place while everything that once made the place intelligible begins to vanish. Streets endure, buildings survive, names remain attached to maps, yet the internal coordinates have shifted. Mottek87 understand that structural change is experienced privately before it becomes a statistic. One person sees cleaner air and redevelopment; another sees an entire vocabulary of work, class, habit, and belonging becoming obsolete. The music keeps that anger on a short leash. Prominent guitars recall Escape with Romeo and Pink Turns Blue, while the rhythm section has the economical discipline associated with early German post-punk and the sterner corners of Neue Deutsche Welle. Jürgen W.’s vocals lend the songs a dry Ruhr directness, carrying alienation without theatrical anguish. The arrangements leave considerable open space, which makes every bass movement and guitar phrase feel unusually exposed. Standout track Widerstand in particular has a rousing, sing-song chorus channeling Interpol. Emotional intelligence sprouts from tension. Blossoms appear where dust once gathered, lungs clear, and the protective armor accumulated over decades becomes increasingly cumbersome. Improvement carries its own insult when it arrives after the world that required such protection has already been dismantled. “Kleinkunst is about realizing that change is not automatically freedom,” says the band. “Sometimes something gets better, and you still need time to stop being angry about it.” Mottek87 record in a downtown Duisburg apartment with the shutters deliberately closed, sealing themselves off from the city they are attempting to understand. The method suits Kleinkunst. Resistance, in Mottek87’s hands, becomes less a heroic posture than an old reflex whose usefulness has become uncertain: a form of emotional muscle memory inherited from a place that keeps changing faster than its people can decide what they are prepared to surrender. items.body: Hot gun, our promise bleeds You would never stop looking for me Have we left it all behind? Is it lust that’s holding the line? Intimacy becomes especially cruel once its gestures outlive the feeling that gave them meaning. A touch continues out of habit, desire reports for duty, and two people repeat the same private choreography while looking through each other as if they have never met. “Sex Machines,” the latest single from Dutch brothers Ruben and Matthijs Pol, occupies that bleakly comic interval, where lust keeps the body busy after the relationship has already vacated the premises. Following a single launch show during Paris Fashion Week in June, Pol now give that estrangement a public face in the song’s official video, directed by fashion photographer and filmmaker Rémi Lamandé. The duo treats New Wave as a living language, bringing music, fashion, moving image, and performance into the same sharpened frame. Here, a lovers’ closed loop becomes a roving interview program whose strangers seem to know every private detail. The song advances on twitching beats, serrated guitars, and clipped vocals, with each syllable inspected, stamped, and sent down the conveyor belt. Sparks supplies the arch pop theatre, while DEVO’s mechanized discipline tightens the arrangement into nervous obedience. Sigue Sigue Sputnik adds tabloid chrome and cheap-thrill futurism; Adam and the Ants lend the proceedings enough rouge, regalia, and heroic excess to turn emotional collapse into prime-time entertainment. Through it all, the robotic chant of “we are sex machines” passes from come-on to diagnosis. Lamandé opens the video in daylight, where a striped-sleeved interviewer, Ruben Pol, carries a star-marked microphone through a narrow service alley. An elderly woman in a floral dress, a woman in pink, a muscled, semi-shirtless man wearing an enormous silver “S,” and several other passersby take their turns before the camera. They offer no opinions or explanations; instead, each stranger lip-syncs Pol’s account of physical appetite and emotional vacancy. Stark title cards and white-background close-ups give the sequence the air of a public-information broadcast commandeered by style and libido. The assignment soon strays underground. The cast descends into a concrete parking garage, crowds the reporter, gathers around a car, and carries a cardboard placard commanding viewers to REPENT. Pol eventually perform before a packed room and a hard white backlight as the same faces press toward the handheld camera. What began as an orderly street interview becomes a collective compulsion, collapsing the distance between observer, participant, stranger, and former lover. A final outtake catches the brothers laughing together, briefly breaking the program’s immaculate pose. “It started off with the idea of doing an interview style video with a diverse cast of characters,” the band explain. “We liked the idea of ‘strangers’ singing the song, similarly how the two ex-lovers in the lyrics are acting like strangers. We shared the idea with director Remi Lamandé who brought the full script to life.” Watch the video for Sex Machines below: “Sex Machines” is available through Bandcamp and other streaming platforms. Listen below, and order here. Sex Machines by Pol Pol introduced their analogue-driven edge with a self-titled debut EP in 2023. The subsequent singles “Masks” and “The Chameleon” moved deeper into theatrical New Romantic territory, establishing the brothers as musicians whose presentation carries as much intent as the recordings themselves. The duo oversees their visuals, videos, merchandise, and fanzines themselves. Their first zine, documenting a Western European tour, is stocked by the Paris bookshop Librairie 1909. That multidisciplinary practice has also led to sound-design collaborations with Louis Vuitton, Miu Miu, and others. In early 2026, Pol opened sold-out Lebanon Hanover shows in London, Lille, and Paris. With “Sex Machines,” their private machinery has moved into public view, microphone extended and camera rolling, only to discover that the whole crowd already knows the refrain. items.body:
The legend behind Eurobeat anthem ‘Pump Up The Jam’ does folk and goth-pop in a fairly corny delivery from Stroom

After cropping up on a compilation EP (STREP-039) last year with the brooding balm of ‘Ambient Kinsky’, Jo Bogaert aka Thomas De Quincey (and tonnes more monikers) ‘fesses up to these languid and pretty cheesy cuts dating to his early years, spanning the Lemmiwinks-like strums and vox of ‘I Want You To Know Me’ and the prog-folk of ‘I Hear A Whale Song’ as part of White Light alongside Johan Guns, Kris Michiels, and Toon Vantilborgh, while the other two come from his 1983 solo album ‘None Of Them Are Green’, and follow his nose for black clad goth-rock and pop strums, including the vinegary strokes of ‘So Obscene.’
items._cn_summary: 该专辑收录乔·博格尔特早年创作的一组作品，其中两首出自他与约翰·冈斯、克里斯·米歇尔斯、托恩·范蒂尔博赫组成的白光线乐队，另两首来自其1983年的个人专辑。音乐以民谣拨弦和哥特流行、哥特摇滚为基底，带有前卫民谣的倾向，人声与吉他编排松弛慵懒，部分段落显得直白甚至俗气，但整体在暗调氛围中保留了旧式独立制作的粗糙质感。作为对这位多面手音乐人早期脉络的补全，这张合辑展示了他在主流舞曲之外对民谣与暗黑流行风格的兴趣，也让人看到其创作谱系的另一侧面。

items.body: Yazoo, the English synthpop duo of Vince Clarke and Alison Moyet, released their debut album “Upstairs at Eric’s” on 20 August 1982 through Mute Records. The album turns 44 this year. It reached number two on the UK Albums Chart and was later certified platinum by the British Phonographic Industry. How Yazoo recorded ‘Upstairs at Eric’s’ The title points at Eric Radcliffe, who ran Blackwing Studios in London, where the sessions took place. Radcliffe produced the record with Yazoo and engineered it with John Fryer. Daniel Miller, the Mute founder who signed the duo, added production. Clarke wrote seven of the eleven tracks: “Don’t Go,” “Too Pieces,” “Bad Connection,” “I Before E Except After C,” “In My Room,” “Only You” and “Tuesday.” Moyet wrote the other four: “Midnight,” “Goodbye 70’s,” “Winter Kills” and “Bring Your Love Down (Didn’t I).” Two UK top-three singles, “Only You” and “Don’t Go,” had already charted before the album arrived. Clarke had left Depeche Mode after that band’s 1981 debut “Speak & Spell,” and the pair came together through an advertisement Moyet placed in Melody Maker. Moyet has described what she was looking for at the time: “I put an ad in Melody Maker looking for a semi-professional band […] Not someone who’d just had a massive hit album.” The two had known each other since their school years in Basildon, Essex. Clarke recalled taking the duo’s first recording to Miller, and getting a reading he misjudged: “I took the demo to Daniel Miller at Mute, and I got the distinct impression he was not interested. ‘That’s that,’ I thought. ‘Get a proper job’.” Clarke has described the sessions themselves as unplanned: “Nobody really knew what they were doing. We were open to trying anything – it was like being in a toy shop, finding out what would happen if you pressed different buttons.” In North America the album appeared under the name Yaz, on Sire Records. Mute issued a remastered edition in 2008, the version now on streaming services, alongside the “In Your Room” box set and the duo’s Reconnected tour. About Yazoo Yazoo formed in Basildon, Essex, in late 1981, with Clarke on keyboards and Moyet on vocals and piano. Mute released their first single, “Only You,” in May 1982; it reached number two on the UK Singles Chart. “Don’t Go” followed and entered the UK top five, and “Upstairs at Eric’s” arrived on 20 August 1982. The duo toured Britain that year as the Guided Tour, and in 1983 won the Brit Award for British Breakthrough Act alongside a nomination for British Group. The partnership did not survive the second album. Clarke and Moyet split in May 1983, before “You and Me Both” reached shops. Moyet began a solo career with “Alf” in 1984; Clarke co-founded The Assembly, then formed Erasure with Andy Bell in 1985. A quarter of a century later the two reconciled, reissuing both studio albums with the “In Your Room” box set and touring the UK, Europe and North America in 2008 as Reconnected, documented on the 2010 live album “Reconnected Live.” They shared a stage again in May 2011, performing three Yazoo songs at a festival organised by Mute. Side-Line has since covered Clarke’s first solo album in Vince Clarke launches debut solo album ‘Songs of Silence’ – Out now, the archive footage in The last Depeche Mode show with Vince Clarke – Watch it now, and a recent reworking of the duo’s final single in Yazoo hit ‘Nobody’s Diary’ gets Sgt Slick rework – Out now. Forty-four years on, “Upstairs at Eric’s” remains the first of the two albums the duo completed together.
items._cn_summary: Yazoo 的首张专辑《Upstairs at Eric's》于1982年由 Mute 发行，由 Vince Clarke 与 Alison Moyet 组成。专辑在伦敦 Blackwing Studios 录制，标题取自工程师 Eric Radcliffe。Clarke 创作了七首曲目，Moyet 创作了四首，两人通过 Moyet 在 Melody Maker 刊登的广告结识。专辑中的《Only You》和《Don't Go》成为英国热门单曲，并推动专辑达到英国榜第二。制作上以模拟合成器与 Moyet 的蓝调嗓音为核心，Clarke 形容录音过程像在玩具店里尝试各种按钮，带有即兴探索的开放感。该专辑被视为早期合成器流行的重要作品，其简洁的旋律和电子音色影响了后来的电子音乐场景。2008年 Mute 发行了重制版，使当代听众仍能接触到这一经典录音。

items.body: Los Angeles post-punk band Deceits have released a video for “One Day You’ll Hurt As Much As Me”, the single issued on 25 March 2026 as their first release for Get Better Records. Raquel Rojas directed the clip. The band have also confirmed the Hurt As Much As Me Tour 2026, a 17-date North American run opening on 24 September at Slowdown in Omaha, Nebraska. The single pairs the studio version with a second take listed as “One Day You’ll Hurt As Much As Me (Studio Demo 2025)”. Both tracks are available through Bandcamp, and the single is also on Spotify and Apple Music. Everything Deceits issued before this point was self-released, which makes the Get Better Records single the first record the band have put out through a label. The band describe the track in terms of a slow-burning break rather than a sudden one: “It’s a dark, cathartic anthem about heartbreak and betrayal, not the sudden kind, but the slow, devastating kind that lingers.” Musically the song runs on a melodic bass figure, a dance-tempo hi-hat pattern and a sustained guitar line, with Kevin Moreno’s vocal carrying the title phrase as a repeated cadence. It sits close to the The Cure and Bauhaus reference points the band have named for their own records. Rojas builds the video around an Amtrak journey along the Pacific coast. Moreno and drummer Francisco Saenz ride the train while Gustavo Alexander Moreno and Logan Martinez appear as their childhood counterparts in beach and station footage, and performance scenes place the pair in a chain-link pedestrian overpass beside the tracks. One Day You’ll Hurt As Much As Me by DECEITS Deceits tour dates for autumn 2026 Computer Kill support the first twelve shows. Haunt Me join for the two Florida dates, where Computer Kill do not appear. The run closes with three California shows, including one with Christian Death in Ocean Beach and an appearance at Darker Waves Festival alongside Morrissey, Simple Minds, Gary Numan and Smashing Pumpkins. 24 September – Omaha, NE, USA – Slowdown 26 September – Davenport, IA, USA – Raccoon Motel 27 September – Chicago, IL, USA – Sleeping Village 28 September – Hamtramck, MI, USA – Small’s 30 September – Somerville, MA, USA – The Rockwell 1 October – Troy, NY, USA – No Fun 3 October – Philadelphia, PA, USA – The Grape 4 October – Brooklyn, NY, USA – Woodshop 5 October – Washington, DC, USA – Pearl Street Warehouse 6 October – Durham, NC, USA – Stanczyks Music Bar 7 October – Charlotte, NC, USA – Snug Harbor 8 October – Atlanta, GA, USA – Purgatory 10 October – Fort Lauderdale, FL, USA – Revolution Live / Hells Gate Festival 11 October – Orlando, FL, USA – Will’s Pub 28 October – West Hollywood, CA, USA – The Roxy Theatre 13 November – Ocean Beach, CA, USA – The Holding Company 14 November – Huntington Beach, CA, USA – Darker Waves Festival Mind’s Eye and Camp Blu open the Roxy Theatre show. Ticket links are listed on the band’s own shows page. About Deceits Deceits formed in Los Angeles in 2021 around longtime friends Kevin “Puppy” Moreno, who handles vocals and instruments, and Francisco “Sisco” Saenz on drums and percussion. The band mix post-punk and gothic rock with the rhythmic and melodic habits of the Spanish-language music both members grew up with, and they perform with an all-analogue live setup. The group first put out a run of self-released singles, later collected as the cassette compilation “Primeros Recuerdos”, which gathers “Every Promise”, “Failures”, “En Soledad”, “Fate (Is When I’m With You)” and “Guiding Light”. The debut album “If There’s No Heaven…” followed on 3 November 2023 and appeared on 12-inch black vinyl, 12-inch gold vinyl, cassette and jewel-case CD. Alex Estrada engineered and mixed the album at Pale Moon Ranch, Will Killingsworth mastered it at Dead Air Studios, and James Edwards of Male Tears contributed additional engineering. Bruxa of Heskeblad and Silver & Steel Artworks supplied the artwork, with logo and layout by Sean McCormack. The album credits list a three-piece lineup of Moreno on vocals, bass and keyboards, Kevin Hernandez on guitar and keyboards, and Saenz on drums. Deceits have named The Cure, Sad Lovers & Giants, The Chameleons and The Danse Society among the records that shaped it. Two further singles followed, “Please, Wake Up” and the 7-inch “All We Are (Are Memories)”, the latter issued with remixes by Vacios Cuerpos, Give My Remains To Broadway, 60 juno and Casket Cassette. The band have shared bills with She Past Away, She Wants Revenge, New Order and Anja Huwe of Xmal Deutschland. “One Day You’ll Hurt As Much As Me” is the band’s first release for Get Better Records, and the video and the autumn tour are the first campaign built around it.
items._cn_summary: 洛杉矶后朋克乐队Deceits通过Get Better Records发行单曲《One Day You’ll Hurt As Much As Me》，这是他们首次经由厂牌发布的作品。歌曲以旋律化贝斯线、舞曲节奏的踩镲与持续吉他音线构建暗色基底，主唱以重复性唱段强化标题所传达的缓慢心碎感，乐队自述其主题更接近一种绵长而毁灭性的背叛与失恋，而非骤然断裂。音乐参照系指向The Cure与Bauhaus，整体处于经典后朋克/哥特传统之内。视频由Raquel Rojas执导，以太平洋沿岸的Amtrak列车之旅为线索，穿插乐队成员与童年扮演者的海滩和车站画面，并在轨道旁的人行天桥拍摄表演场景。单曲另收录2025年录音室小样版本，数字平台均已上线。乐队同时公布2026年秋季北美巡演日程，共17场，部分场次由Computer Kill与Haunt Me助阵，最后一站包括Darker Waves Festival。作为一篇偏重发行与巡演信息的报道，文章对音乐本身的描述有限，但作品风格定位明确，适合后朋克与暗潮乐迷关注。

items.body: Two days before the album lands, Black Marble has released a video for “It Always Comes to Me”, the last advance single from “Life in Small Spaces”. The fifth Black Marble album arrives on 21 August 2026 through Sacred Bones Records on CD and on transparent orange vinyl. Claes Nordwall directed the video. Chris Stewart, the project’s sole member since 2016, follows the release with a North American tour opening on 22 August in Santa Ana, California. “It Always Comes to Me” opens the record. Stewart explains the song as a study of somebody who keeps getting away with things: “It Always Comes to Me is about a cool, calm, collected person who seems to always be able to get away with things other people can’t, either by charm or deceit,” he stated. “Like a modern version of The Kinks’ Dedicated Follower of Fashion, the song doesn’t explicitly advocate for or condemn this kind of behaviour, but takes a birds eye view of it as the protagonist moves through the world. Ultimately, it leaves it up to the listener to judge for themselves. The subject of the song seems to be having fun but can it last? And how much does our judgement really matter either way?” Bass and guitar carry more of the arrangement here than the layered synthesizers of earlier Black Marble records. Stewart has described what he wanted from the album’s guitar parts as an attempt to “create this chime-y hypnotic quality. Like a radio dial that is between two stations.” Nordwall filmed Stewart moving through New York subways, bridges, basketball courts and pool halls. The director connected that pacing to Finnish cinema: “I was drawn to the idea of a character moving through the modern world on his own timeline,” he stated. “While everything around him races forward, he remains quietly rooted in who he is. I was inspired by Chris’s ideas behind the album which made me think of the dry stoicism of Aki Kaurismäki’s films. I wanted to make something that celebrates resilience, character and the beauty of refusing to chase the next thing.” Life in Small Spaces by Black Marble “Life in Small Spaces” runs eleven tracks across two sides. Side one holds “It Always Comes To Me”, “Jim Carol New Year”, “Anything”, “Get Back Up”, “Other Man’s Dream” and “Guess”. Side two holds “Life Without”, “Missing History”, “Panopticon Calls”, “Picture When” and “Sonny Boy”. Side-Line covered the earlier single from the album when Black Marble shared “Anything” and set “Life in Small Spaces” on 18 July 2026. Black Marble tour dates for 2026 The tour runs from 22 August to 19 September 2026. The Serfs and Public Circuit open selected dates, with Jimmy Cicero on some shows. 22 August – Santa Ana, CA, USA – Constellation Room at the Observatory 23 August – Los Angeles, CA, USA – 1720 25 August – San Francisco, CA, USA – Rickshaw Stop 26 August – Sacramento, CA, USA – Harlow’s 28 August – Seattle, WA, USA – The Crocodile 29 August – Portland, OR, USA – Wonder Ballroom 30 August – Boise, ID, USA – Shrine Social Club 31 August – Salt Lake City, UT, USA – Urban Lounge 1 September – Denver, CO, USA – The Federal Theatre 3 September – Omaha, NE, USA – Slowdown 4 September – Minneapolis, MN, USA – Fine Line 5 September – Chicago, IL, USA – Thalia Hall 6 September – Detroit, MI, USA – El Club 7 September – Toronto, ON, Canada – Lee’s Palace 8 September – Montreal, QC, Canada – La Sala Rosa 10 September – New York City, NY, USA – Webster Hall 11 September – Philadelphia, PA, USA – Union Transfer 12 September – Baltimore, MD, USA – Ottobar 14 September – Raleigh, NC, USA – Kings 15 September – Atlanta, GA, USA – The Earl 17 September – Houston, TX, USA – White Oak Music Hall Upstairs 18 September – Dallas, TX, USA – Club Dada 19 September – Austin, TX, USA – 29th Street Ballroom About Black Marble Chris Stewart started Black Marble in Brooklyn in 2011 with Ty Kube of Team Robespierre. Sub Pop imprint Hardly Art signed the project after Stewart posted a single song online, and the debut album “A Different Arrangement” appeared on 9 October 2012. The second album, “It’s Immaterial”, followed in October 2016 on Ghostly International and marked Kube’s exit, leaving Stewart as the sole member. Stewart moved to Sacred Bones Records and relocated from Brooklyn to Los Angeles around the third album, “Bigger Than Life”, released on 25 October 2019. The covers EP “I Must Be Living Twice” came in August 2020 with reworkings of songs originally by Wire, Robert Palmer and Grouper. A fourth full-length, “Fast Idol”, arrived on 22 October 2021, also on Sacred Bones. “Anything”, issued on 17 July 2026 with a video by Scott Kiernan, previewed “Life in Small Spaces” a month before release. “It Always Comes to Me” closes the run-up to the album’s arrival on 21 August 2026 and the tour that starts the following day.
items._cn_summary: Black Marble的新专辑《Life in Small Spaces》将于2026年8月21日通过Sacred Bones发行，收录11首曲目。先行单曲《It Always Comes to Me》作为专辑开场曲，以贝斯和吉他为主导，减少了早期作品中的层叠合成器，追求一种介于电台频道之间的叮当催眠质感。歌曲主题描绘一个凭借魅力或欺骗总能逃脱惩罚的人物，灵感源自The Kinks的《Dedicated Follower of Fashion》，但保持中立视角，将判断留给听众。由Claes Nordwall执导的MV拍摄于纽约地铁、桥梁、球场和台球厅，导演以芬兰导演阿基·考里斯马基式的克制与静止感来呈现主角在加速世界中的自我节奏。专辑发行后随即展开北美巡演。
