items.album: JACK BRUCE Songs For A Tailor (Jazz Rock/Fusion, 1969)
items.excerpt: Review by BrufordFreak — The highly-revered bass player's first solo album release finds Jack supported in part by members of Colosseum (Dick Heckstall-Smith and Jon Hiseman), in part Nucleus (Chris Spedding and drummer John Marshall). Bruce was, of course, a former member of Cream (with guitarist Eric Clapton and drummer Ginger Baker), Manfred Mann, John Mayall's Bluesbreakers (with Eric Clapton), and both the Graham Bond Organization (with Baker and Heckstall-Smith) and Graham Bond Quart
items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — The highly-revered bass player's first solo album release finds Jack supported in part by members of Colosseum (Dick Heckstall-Smith and Jon Hiseman), in part Nucleus (Chris Spedding and drummer John Marshall). Bruce was, of course, a former member of Cream (with guitarist Eric Clapton and drummer Ginger Baker), Manfred Mann, John Mayall's Bluesbreakers (with Eric Clapton), and both the Graham Bond Organization (with Baker and Heckstall-Smith) and Graham Bond Quartet (with Baker and guitarist John McLaughlin) as well as Alexis Korner's Blues Incorporated (his first collaboration with Baker and Heckstall-Smith). The material that became Songs for a Tailor was recorded in London in April and May of 1969 and then released in Britain by Polydor Records on August 29 of 1969 (Oct. 6 in the States by ATCO). 1. "Never Tell Your Mother She's Out of Tune" (3:41) R&B Brass Rock with a complex syncopated construction that uses dissonant chords from both the horn section as well as an unusual progression for the odd vocal melody to sing over. The drumming is particularly tight but it's the horn arrangements that really knock your socks off. Jack's bass playing is impressive, especially toward the end when he starts to stray outside the main riff he created to found the song over. Not a great nor memorable song except for the unusual horn arrangements. (8.875/10)2. "Theme for an Imaginary Western" (3:30) sounding like a PROCOL HARUM song with both vocal melody, band's chord progression, organ and piano dominance, and pace, Jack's voice has a kind of jazzy VAN MORRISON quality and styling to it. Another okay song. (8.75/10)3. "Tickets to Water Falls" (3:00) a brief piano intro turns into another unusual jazzy song with a bit of a Caribbean flavor to it despite its loud free-flowing Jazz-Rock bass and multiple keyboards and spicy rhythm guitar (which Chris Spedding later turns into a bit of a George Harrison-like solo). Very interesting. (8.875/10)4. "Weird of Hermiston" (2:24) a Blues-Rock based song that again crosses into that area of music that is more commonly traversed by artists like Van Morrison, The Band, Jethro Tull, and George Harrison--this might even be considered proto-Americana! (8.75/10)5. "Rope Ladder to the Moon" (2:54) a Blues-Rock song that sounds very much like it could have come from one of JETHRO TULL's earliest albums. I like this one. Even the vocal sounds as quirky and adventurous as something Ian Anderson (or Van Morrison) would do. (8.875/10)6. "The Ministry of Bag" (2:49) this one is pure Memphis Blues--as if Booker T & The M.G.'s and The Memphis Horns are on board from start to finish. Jack's singing is aggressive and bluesy like young Dr. John or Wilson Pickett. A top three song. (9/10)7. "He the Richmond" (3:36) Jack's strumming acoustic guitar opens this where he is joined by John Marshall's drums and his own bass while singing a vocal as if channelling a combination of Richie Havens, Ian Anderson, and Dr. John. The uncredited harmonizing vocals of the second minute are really unusual--and cool! A top three song for me. (9/10)8. "Boston Ball Game 1967" (1:45) loud horns and pounding piano dominate this one so much that Jack's multiple vocal(s) tracks are nearly drowned out (and seem to have to force themselves to be heard). Kind of cool but could've been turned into something more. (Or else.) (4.375/5)9. "To Isengard" (5:28) acoustic guitars strumming and picking while multiple vocal lines are tracking--the lead using a delicate, high-pitched timbre (that sounds like Rod Stewart trying to sing up high). Very interesting. I really like the vocal harmonies as well as the interplay between Jack and Chris' two guitars. At 3:15 there is a brief stop out of which explodes a uptempo motif that spreads things out among bass, drums, and the psychedelic sound creations and play of Chris Spedding's electric guitar. While I prefer the first half, I did enjoy the second half, too. My final top three song. (8.875/10)10. "The Clearout" (2:35) trying to go back to the Cream world? Heavy power chords from both electric guitar and bass over Jon Hiseman's Ginger Baker-like militaristic drumming. Not my favorite use of these talented artist's skills. And I didn't even mention the Roger Daltry-like singing or lyrics over the Beatles' "Birthday"-like melody line. (8.75/10)Total time 31:42Jack can certainly impress with his bass playing--as if he could be the father of Jaco Pastorius--but his active and jazzy lines (and sound) are not always as fitting to the music and his vocal stylings and lyrics aren't quite the kind of stuff for the AM charts. B/four stars; while I definitely appreciate the uniqueness of Jack's talents and vision, I find most of the music on this album to be almost confusing and messy, and the lyrics to be nearly impregnable and, probably, written from a very personal, albeit creative perspective (not unlike those of Van Morrison).

items._cn_summary: 这张1969年的专辑是Jack Bruce离开Cream后的首张个人作品，邀请了Colosseum和Nucleus等乐队的乐手参与录制。乐评对每首曲目进行了逐曲分析，指出作品融合了爵士摇滚、蓝调摇滚和复杂和声编排，如铜管组的不和谐和弦运用、加勒比风味节奏以及多样化的键盘配置。部分歌曲被比作Procol Harum、Jethro Tull和Van Morrison的风格，也有孟菲斯蓝调的演绎。贝斯演奏被多次称赞，尤其在偏离主riff时的即兴表现。整体而言，这是一张跨越多种风格的爵士摇滚专辑，编曲有一定复杂度，但内容更偏向传统摇滚框架内的融合，与极端前卫或实验音乐的距离较远。

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评聚焦于约翰·柯川的《Ascension》，指出该专辑在风格上与广受欢迎的《A Love Supreme》形成强烈反差。文中提到，在录制此专辑前不久，柯川还在演奏《Nature Boy》和《Chim Chim Cheree》这类相对传统、带有流行色彩的作品，但激进的音乐探索已逐渐显现。评论将《Ascension》视为一次冲击性的转折，呈现了从主流抒情爵士向极端自由即兴的过渡，乐手之间的集体即兴结构成为核心表达方式。该作记录了柯川挣脱传统调性与和声框架的过程，对自由爵士与前卫即兴的发展具有标志性意义，适合对先锋爵士演变历程感兴趣的听众进一步了解。

items.body: Oslo duo Rule Of Two release the six-track EP “Restoring Balance to a Broken World” on August 27, 2026 through the Madrid label Polypiel Records. The record gathers the singles the pair have issued across 2026 and adds one previously unreleased track, “Decompression”. It follows their debut album, “Aiming For the Sun”, from November 2025. The running order is “Call For Aid”, “All Time Low”, “Decompression”, “It’s No Good”, “Hole In The Ground” and “Afterlife”. Rule Of Two wrote and recorded the music, Ronny Flissundet wrote the lyrics, and the EP was mixed and mastered at Crystal Island Studios in Nesodden, Norway. “It’s No Good” is a Depeche Mode cover, reworked as darkwave and industrial electronics. The release is digital. Five of the six tracks reached listeners first as standalone singles. Side-Line covered “All Time Low” in February 2026, then “Afterlife” on May 7, the duo’s first single for Polypiel. “It’s No Good” arrived on June 4 and “Hole In The Ground” on July 16. That last single is the loudest thing on the EP. The band describe it on Bandcamp as “an intense yet catchy electronic blowout with punkrock mentality lurking in the background, describing an impossible situation and the overwhelming urge of escaping it, preferably through a hole in the ground.” Kristian Liljan directed its video. Hole In The Ground by Rule Of Two About Rule Of Two Rule Of Two are Ronny Flissundet and Kristian Liljan, formed in Oslo in 2023. Both came out of the Norwegian underground rock and metal scene through Damokles, KITE and Dunderbeist. Flissundet handles lyrics, vocals, guitars and synths; Liljan handles beats, loops, bass, synths, production and the band’s videos. On stage the project expands to a five-piece, and the duo have played a handful of Norwegian shows. The band call themselves a cyberpunk-indie-electronic outfit with a darkwave edge, and name Nine Inch Nails, Depeche Mode, Carpenter Brut and Crosses among their reference points alongside hardcore punk and classical music. In practice that comes out as darkwave and synthpop with indie pop and post-punk running underneath. They built the catalogue single by single from 2023 onward, releasing more than twenty of them plus the EPs “Drowning”, “Echoes” and “Dancing Drone”, the collection “Scraps & Pieces”, and covers of Nirvana’s “Something In The Way” and Ghost’s “Monstrance Clock”. Side-Line covered the arrival of the debut album “Aiming For the Sun”, issued on November 13, 2025. The Polypiel run started in May 2026 and has produced three singles in ten weeks. “Restoring Balance to a Broken World” closes that sequence and puts it on one release, with “Decompression” as the track that has not been heard before.

items.body: It’s been a minute since we last heard from jazz guitarist Brad Farberman and his experimental jazz-funk band, Middle Blue, but as you’ll hear on this new Island House Recordings release, it was indeed very much worth the wait. Available today on cassette and digital, Let’s Name a Star on Friday Night is a supremely fun jam record with a bright insatiable energy and heaps of swagger. The album bops with vivacious beats, squealing, honking sax, stanky bass lines and fat wah-wah drenched guitar lines. On tracks like the title cut, soaring melodic clarinets shines side by side with some dirty sax solos, slick drumming and deliciously warped rhythm guitar. As soon as the funky groove of this song catches your ear, it does not let go. This is jazz that is guaranteed for good times. Put this album on when you have company over, and the mood will stay highly elevated til you reach the end…before you inevitably flip the tape over and replay it again and again. If you’re a fan of Joe McPhee, Bobbi Humphrey and Herbie Mann’s work with Sonny Sharrock, then just click here right now to get your copy of this total blast of a record today. -KH
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由吉他手Brad Farberman领衔的Middle Blue乐队带来，是一张以爵士放克为骨架的欢快即兴作品。专辑收录卡带与数字版本，音色明亮且充满活力，吉他采用浓郁的哇音效果铺陈节奏线，贝斯线条粗粝脏厚，萨克斯则以尖锐的嘶吼式吹奏与高音单簧管的旋律并置，形成戏剧化对话。鼓组滑溜灵动，整张专辑维持着放克律动的连贯推进，几乎每一首都拒绝松手。据乐评描述，同名曲将单簧管悠扬旋律与肮脏萨克斯独奏并行展开，营造出让人忍不住反复翻面重听的高涨氛围。厂牌Island House Recordings属小型独立厂牌，文章将其与Joe McPhee、Herbie Mann及Sonny Sharrock的跨界合作相提并论，暗示其在实验爵士脉络中的位置。

items.body: Our cores may have rotted into compost over the summer, but we’ve been churned into the earth and emerged with a collection of releases to share that have given us life this year. I tasked a few of our writers with narrowing down a top 10 for 2026 within a specific sub-genre I knew they’re into, highlighting specifically their number 1 thus far with a brief write-up. Through this we have a hefty list of  forty LPs/EPs, highlighting the best of metalcore/mathcore, screamo/post-hardcore, grindcore, and noise rock that this year has served up so far. So, let’s get to it, and we hope you find some new filth to bask in. -TBPK Shares Their Top 10 Metalcore/Mathcore Releases So Far This YearConverge - Hum of Hurt / Love Is Not Enough I've put the Converge surprise double release of Hum of Hurt and Love Is Not Enough together on this list at number 1...but really that is a bit of a cheat on my part. Hum of Hurt is by far the more emotive, ambitious offering of the two, sitting nicely alongside previous full lengths The Dusk In Us and All We Love We Leave Behind. Standout tracks such as "Detonator" and "Doom in Bloom" are Converge at their brooding, progressive best (and I love that we get to hear Nate's vocals, as a new Doomriders record looks unlikely any time soon). Don't get me wrong, Love Is Not Enough has some killer moments (the title track and "Bad Faith" being two he of them), and it's immensely enjoyable, but overall feels like a slightly one dimensional version of Converge instead of the more complex and multilayered band they've matured into over the last fifteen years. All that being said, we got TWO new Converge albums this year and that makes me very happy indeed.  Hum of Hurt by Converge Chamber - this is goodbye Merit - Sweetness Fades Crowquill - Erase The FilesKicked in the Head by a Horse - BLOOM/DECAY .Gif From God - Dissimulation A Knife in the Dark - Songs Without WitnessThe Absolute Worst or The Absolute Worst - calculusZao - Pillars Temple Guard - Citadel In Flames Crouch - Breaking the Catatonic State This album ended up falling between the cracks on our ‘Best so far’ coverage as it didn't fit into any of our designated genres (we might need to add a ‘Sludge’ list for 2027). It would've been sacrilege to leave it out completely, especially as it's one of my favourite releases of the year so far.It has been well documented that Crouch features members of Oathbreaker and Wiegedood, but it's clear that one of the main influences pulsing through Breaking the Catatonic State is the criminally underrated Knut. Oh how I love Knut. 2002's Challenger is damn near a perfect album in my eyes. This Belgian trio clearly also worship at the altar of the Swiss sludgecore titans, as they effortlessly mix filthy downtuned riffage with slick technicality and clever use of samples. You'll hear some other tips of the cap from 2000's hardcore royalty, such as Coalesce, Converge and Botch in here too. All of these influences have something in common; a resolute anger. That is what fuels everything on this debut full length and the band finds new ways to implement their venom across its ten chapters. I implore you to listen to the whole album from start to finish, but there are a few tracks that stand out. “Vidal” showcases just how musically tight these guys are with a series of complex staccato compositions. “Twisted Colossus” is an absolute monster and does exactly what it says on the tin, but then throws in a wonderful detour that takes the track into unexpected jazz territory. The longest and slowest track on the record crushes everything in its path, and no, I don't think it's a coincidence that this track is titled “Geneva”. The Knut worship may have had me hooked from the start, but the sheer quality of this debut album is difficult to dispute, even for those who don't normally like sludgy hardcore. Without a doubt one of the highlights of 2026 so far.  Breaking The Catatonic State by Crouch JD shares their Top 10 Noise Rock Releases So Far This YearDoppler - Pourquoi ce disque ?In terms of sonic scope, compositional prowess, and progressive approaches, few noise rock releases this year have stood up to Pourquoi ce disque ? by Doppler. It’s true that Mandy, Indiana’s newest is one of the most sonically innovative and unsettling noise rock albums I’ve heard in a while, and, if I’m being honest, Zu’s take on noise rock is actually complex hard prog with a healthy dose of dissonance. But I still can’t get over Doppler’s brilliant, labyrinthine songwriting. “Incipit Expicit” is an early example on their 2026 release, as the song transitions from swinging, odd-metered noise rock to post-punk reggae. The song then swerves into a lengthy, driving climax that gradually builds in tension before exploding into unbridled fury. Aside from the meticulously composed songs, the album has an emotional depth beyond the visceral anger prevalent on most noise rock albums. There is an air of Queens of the Stone Age-like playfulness during the closing solo in “Of Pieces of Break.” That track is juxtaposed against the subsequent ruminative restraint of instrumental “Piano Cassé,” which features a nearly meditative percussionless interplay between the guitar and bass for half of the song’s running time. These sonic and emotional explorations illustrate a musical ambition that makes Pourquoi ce disque ? one of the most engaging listens of the year, and not just within the noise rock genre. Pourquoi Ce Disque ? by DOPPLER Mandy, Indiana - URGHHammok - When Does This Place Become Our SceneBitter Branches - Let’s Give The Land Back To The AnimalsZu - Ferrum SidereumTruck Violence - The weathervane is my bodyBags Bags Bags - It Eats Me UpAPE AMP - APE AMPThe Freqs - No God on the Gold CoastParts & Labor - Set of All SetsTB Shares their Top 10 Screamo Releases So Far This YearOstraca - ThreadI'm not sure if it says more about this album or this year, but for the first time covering this genre there is an obvious number one album. Thread is another powerful release from one of the brightest names in the genre, showcasing a raw fury of violence and passion that coalesces into something beautiful in a way that is nearly unparalleled right now. Ostraca are a dynamic band, building off the strengths of bands like envy and city of caterpillar before them. However, while there's a similar sense of atmospheric tension-stretching, they double down on the heaviness. In their songwriting this often comes across as a “calm before the storm” of sorts, such as the eerily beautiful acoustic passages in “Song for November”, before exploding into distorted, earth-churning evolutions of those same riffs. They're effective at making these dense walls of heaviness feel earned, with thoughtful bridges which seamlessly carry their passion throughout each song. It’s refreshing when this doesn’t just feel reserved for when they're pushed to the brink. And it’s not just the vocals or the minor ambient riffing, but the way their songwriting brings it all together. If you’re looking for a gut punch of grief and emotional catharsis, it’s hard to find a better band to listen to right now. While generally lumped into the screamo realm, it’s difficult to define them due to their heavy post-metal influence. Not to mention they’re one of few bands in the scene to incorporate lower guttural vocals into their sound. If you’re more into the punk and emo side of the genre this might not be as much of your thing, but it’s hard to deny the transcendental impact of their emotional delivery. Listening to this album on a lengthy solo drive across northern Ontario, I found myself lost in a sort of cinematic nostalgic yearning. Like someone looking through a photo album in a dimly lit room, feeling a thread in your heart slowly start to pull. Somewhere between an existential depression and a pensive contemplation which builds into a fervorous fury. I had the pleasure of seeing Ostraca recently at New Friends Fest in Toronto and was happy to see that these emotions were equally conveyed in their live performance. It seemed to permeate through to the audience both in the softer moments, allowing the crowd to just sink in that weight, ready to erupt into chaos and emotive scream-alongs. An all-around frenzied, engaging and cathartic experience that reflects the essence of their music.  Thread by ostraca Eyelet - SolenoidCassus - Scalis FeldenChalk Hands - The Line That Shapes the Coast of UsThe Saddest Landscape - Alone with HeavenKnumears - DirectionsQuiet Fear - La tierra arriba / El abismo abajoHouse of the Blood Choir - Mom’s AnxietySnag - All the Cages Holding Us Will One Day Turn to DustGros Enfant Mort - Le Sang Des PierresAs Living Arrows - Fragment IJD shares their Top 10 Grindcore Releases So Far This Year (Including Powerviolence, Deathgrind, Mathgrind, Noisegrind, Goregrind, Cybergrind, and Fake Grind)Eastwood - Alle Gegen AlleIn my view, grindcore perfection is often a matter of striking a balance. Too often, grind bands of various stripes end up at one extreme or the other regarding compositions, performances, and production quality. Some overcomplicate songs with endless noodling, whereas others often keep it caveman simple. Some employ an overly clinical approach to production in which the perfectly quantized performances sound lifeless. Some have subpar production values with sloppy performances. In a genre predicated on extremes, this shouldn’t be too surprising; but, in my humble opinion, the sweet spot is when bands strike a balance between those extremes. Eastwood’s Alle Gegen Alle is the best example of this so far this year. The German quartet’s second full-length is full of tightly performed, technically impressive blasts of grindcore coupled with a crystal-clear mix in which the humanness of the performances shines through. The compositions are dense without being overwrought. They rapidly cycle through changes that barely allow the listener to keep their footing, such as the blast-and-mosh tradeoff at the end of “Im Namen des Gehetztes”. But the compositions contain more than enough meat for the listener to chew on, especially as slower tempos and melodic elements peak through from time to time and add some variety, such as in “Alle Gegen Alle” and “Dampfgegart,” respectively. However, the majority of the 11-minute album is, on the whole, visceral and unforgiving. Oh, and did I mention that there is an Assück cover? items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�

items.album: NCN 19: Nik Kershaw, Die Krupps, SKYND, Diary of Dreams and more head to Deutzen

items.body: Nocturnal Culture Night returns to Kulturpark Deutzen from 4 to 6 September 2026, with its traditional Warm-Up taking place on Thursday, 3 September. Now at edition number 19, NCN once again uses several stages to accommodate a programme that reaches well beyond any single definition of goth, industrial or electronic music. The 2026 bill shows that range plainly. Nik Kershaw, Die Krupps, SKYND, Diary of Dreams, Peter Heppner & Band, L’Âme Immortelle, Girls Under Glass, Samsas Traum / Weena Morloch, Siglo XX, Esplendor Geométrico, Pankow, Actors, Sierra Veins, The Beauty Of Gemina, HORSKH, Mildreda, Melotron, Of The Wand & The Moon and Container 90 are the most familiar names on the bill, and they come from very different points in electronic and alternative music history. The festival takes place in Kulturpark Deutzen, roughly 30 kilometres south of Leipzig. NCN stays small by design, with the festival shop describing a capacity of around 2,500 visitors. The programme is spread across the Amphibühne, Waldbühne, Parkbühne and Kulturbühne, alongside the separate Lesebühne. From 300 people to NCN 19 The first Nocturnal Culture Night took place in 2005 with approximately 300 visitors. Holger Troisch had begun developing the idea two years earlier, and that first edition was much smaller than the present festival: one stage and barely a full day of concerts. The growth that followed did not turn NCN into a conventional large festival. Four music stages have been in operation since 2014, while different parts of the programme gradually acquired their own musical emphasis. The Parkbühne, for example, became associated with synth, coldwave, minimal and post-punk from 2016 onwards; the Kulturbühne developed a stronger relationship with neofolk, industrial and experimental work. 2026 is officially NCN 19, while the organisers regard 2027 as the twentieth jubilee edition. The chronology does not correspond directly to twenty consecutive calendar years because there was no regular second edition in 2006 and the pandemic period produced separate special editions. NCN is currently operated through NCN Event GmbH, based in Leipzig, with Holger Troisch remaining the festival’s organiser. Holger Troisch and a festival with no single genre Troisch’s approach to booking explains much of the 2026 programme. Years ago he summarised the balance: “The line-up, the festival lives by big and successful names, but also by insiders.” He followed it with an even simpler statement: “Versatility is important for me.” (Reflections of Darkness, 2017) His more recent comments say the same. Discussing NCN’s identity in 2026, Troisch said that the festival had become too broad musically to tie itself to a single genre, and that introducing new styles was necessary if the event itself was to continue developing. The running order shows that principle more clearly than an alphabetical line-up. On Saturday alone, Nik Kershaw closes the Amphibühne, SKYND headline the Waldbühne, Actors occupy the evening Parkbühne slot, and Esplendor Geométrico close the live programme on the Kulturbühne. Those artists do not belong to one genre or even one generation. They share NCN’s long-standing remit: electronic, post-industrial, dark and alternative music in the broadest sense. Nik Kershaw: an unusual headliner for NCN The most conspicuous name this year is Nik Kershaw, who closes the Amphibühne on Saturday at 22:30. Kershaw’s breakthrough came in 1984, with “Wouldn’t It Be Good”, “I Won’t Let the Sun Go Down on Me” and “The Riddle”. His official biography records 62 weeks on the UK Singles Chart across 1984 and 1985, and he performed at Live Aid in 1985. His later career took in songwriting and production for other artists alongside his own releases and performances. He is not a darkwave or industrial artist, and NCN does not try to redraw his history to make him fit. The festival has long treated the wider electronic and alternative culture of the 1980s as part of its remit rather than limiting itself to artists carrying a particular scene label. Kershaw sits at one end of the festival’s historical spectrum: highly crafted British electronic pop that entered mass culture in the 1980s. Only a few hours earlier, other stages will be presenting EBM, post-punk, industrial electronics and experimental music that developed around or against that same decade. Die Krupps: the industrial line runs directly through Düsseldorf On Sunday the Amphibühne closes with Die Krupps, whose place in this programme needs less explanation. The Düsseldorf group began with the industrial construction of “Stahlwerksinfonie” before “Wahre Arbeit Wahrer Lohn” and subsequent releases developed a hard electronic language closely associated with the foundations of EBM. During the 1990s, metal guitar was folded into that vocabulary, creating the electronic-metal combination that became another major strand of the band’s identity. Die Krupps marked 45 years of activity in 2025. Their current phase is not limited to anniversary performances: the band signed a multi-album agreement with Dependent Records, with a new album announced for 2026, and guitarist Marcel Zürcher returned to the group in June 2026. The band’s own announcement specifically lists NCN among the concerts following his return. There is also a long NCN connection. The festival archive lists Die Krupps in 2015, 2018, 2023 and 2026, making this their fourth appearance in Deutzen. SKYND: industrial music through the architecture of true crime SKYND close Saturday’s Waldbühne at 21:00 and represent a much newer form of industrial performance. The project is built around vocalist SKYND and producer/multi-instrumentalist F, with its catalogue structured around real criminal cases. Rather than using true crime as occasional imagery, the project has made it the organising principle of its music, videos and visual identity. Its own description is simply “TRUE CRIME MUSIC.” The project has released steadily through 2026. Material from “Chapter VII: Red Winter” has included pieces concerning Andrei Chikatilo, Tamara Samsonova and Mikhail Popkov, while the subsequent “Jimmy Savile” opened Chapter VIII: The Open Secret, shifting attention towards institutional protection and the mechanisms that allowed abuse to remain concealed. The NCN set lands in the middle of that run of releases. Diary of Dreams: five appearances across the history of NCN Diary of Dreams play the Waldbühne at 19:25 on Sunday. Adrian Hates’ project has run for more than three decades on electronic production, darkwave structures, guitars and inward songwriting. The current release is “Chapter 1: Dead End Dreams”, while the band continue touring extensively through 2026. Their NCN history is long. The official archive lists appearances in 2007, 2009, 2013, 2021 and 2026, making this their fifth visit. Repeat bookings shape the festival’s history as much as new ones. Some projects come back at intervals long enough for NCN to have documented how their work and their audience changed. Peter Heppner & Band Peter Heppner & Band play the Amphibühne at 17:20 on Sunday, immediately before Die Krupps later that evening. Heppner’s own site confirms the full-band NCN appearance on 6 September 2026. It will be his third NCN, following appearances in 2014 and 2020. Heppner and Die Krupps on the same main stage shows how NCN handles German electronic history. One represents a melodic, vocal-driven lineage closely associated with synthpop and dark pop; the other comes directly from industrial music and EBM. NCN does not collapse those histories into one genre, but it does recognise that their audiences have overlapped for decades. L’Âme Immortelle and Girls Under Glass Friday brings two other established names whose careers have repeatedly crossed the boundaries between electronics, goth and heavier music. L’Âme Immortelle, appearing at 21:25 on the Waldbühne, were founded in Austria in 1996 and are centred on Thomas Rainer and Sonja Kraushofer. The male/female vocal contrast has stayed central to the project while the music itself has moved between dark electronics, rock and more melodic material. The group will mark its 30th anniversary in 2027 with a dedicated concert series. This is their second NCN appearance after 2016. Girls Under Glass, meanwhile, close Friday’s Amphibühne. Their history reaches back to the mid-1980s and encompasses wave, gothic rock, electronics and industrial influences rather than a single fixed style. NCN has hosted them in 2010, 2016, 2022 and now 2026. Siglo XX, Pankow and Esplendor Geométrico: the historically important names are not all on the main stage Some of the historically important bookings are positioned away from the Amphibühne. Belgium’s Siglo XX, appearing at 21:25 on Friday’s Parkbühne, emerged in Genk in 1978 and became an important part of the austere Belgian post-punk and coldwave history of the period. The NCN archive lists 2026 as their first visit to the festival. Pankow, playing Friday on the Waldbühne, represent a different European trajectory. The Florence project developed from the Italian experimental underground into harder electronic and industrial territory and later became strongly associated with EBM. They return to NCN after a previous appearance in 2016. Then there is Esplendor Geométrico, closing Saturday’s Kulturbühne at 22:45. The Spanish project dates to 1980, and its repetitive, physical combination of mechanical rhythm, noise and industrial electronics developed largely outside the Anglo-German narratives through which industrial music is often described. NCN 19 will be their first appearance at the festival. That booking is the kind Troisch’s distinction between “big names” and “insiders” covers: historical weight and billing size are not the same thing. Actors, Sierra Veins, HORSKH and the current generation The contemporary programme Several of the contemporary acts arrive with new material rather than a back catalogue. Canadian ACTORS take the 21:00 Parkbühne slot on Saturday, returning to NCN after their first appearance in 2019. The Vancouver band have released steadily through 2026: “CTRL” appeared in February, followed by the DJ? Acucrack reworking “Dead Inside (Crackmix)” in March, “Left On Read” in April and “Youth” in July. The latter arrives while ACTORS are working on a new album, their first studio record since Acts of Worship and Reanimated. The singles keep the tightly constructed post-punk songwriting the band are known for, but the production hits harder: stronger electronic rhythm, more low-end pressure and a closer relationship with the dancefloor. NCN catches ACTORS mid-change rather than between records. Sierra Veins closes the Parkbühne at 00:10 on Friday, a late slot that suits how far her work now runs past darkwave into techno and harder club music. Her second full-length album, “In The Name Of Blood”, was released on 7 November 2025 and made the change from SIERRA to SIERRA VEINS part of the record’s central subject: identity, inheritance and the traces carried within us. It also includes the collaboration “Memory Cells” with Ghost Dance. In February 2026 she followed it with “HypnoVizion 031: SIERRA VEINS (DJ Mix)”, a 46-minute mix for REZZ’s HypnoVizion series that places her own tracks and remixes beside material from artists including Gesaffelstein, Boys Noize, Matteo Tura and Ghost Dance. The album and the mix place her at NCN with one foot in the dark electronic scene and the other in a much wider club culture. French trio HORSKH open the Parkbühne programme on Friday, three weeks before the release of their new ten-track album “MTNT” on 25 September 2026. Three pieces from this phase have already appeared: “Bad Glitch” in January, “Hyperhuman” in March and “Glow” in June. HORSKH themselves describe the project as neo-industrial / grunge / metal. The new material continues the collision between electronic programming, heavily processed vocals, distorted guitars and industrial rhythm that sets them apart from acts rebuilding an older industrial vocabulary. The NCN set is one of the last festival dates before MTNT is out. Belgium’s Mildreda, appearing on the Waldbühne at 14:20 on Sunday, arrive in Deutzen even closer to a new record. “Realities” is released by Dependent Records on 28 August 2026, just nine days before the NCN performance. The eighteen-track double album follows Blue-Devilled and pushes Jan Dewulf’s dark electro past the colder boundaries usually associated with the genre. The structure expands too: recurring “Reality Check” pieces divide the album, while Johan Van Roy of Suicide Commando appears on “Virtual Goddess” and Constantin “Breñal” Warter of Calva Y Nada guests on “Rückwärts.” The first single, “End of the Line,” appeared in June, followed in July by “Virtual Goddess”; Dewulf has described the latter as a confession rather than a criticism of social media: the contradiction between seeking meaningful connection and still responding to the tiny rewards of digital approval. He also says the writing brought colours and emotions into Mildreda that had sat outside his comfort zone, rather than extending the sound of Blue-Devilled. The NCN set is one of the first chances to hear how that studio material works live, against a show built on Dewulf’s vocals and electronics and Christophe Salvatore’s keyboards. Around them, The Foreign Resort, Mayflower Madame, Winter Severity Index, SIIE, Debdepan, Lovataraxx, Lone Assembly, Grundeis, Container 90, Ambassador 21, Menticide, AD and Intent extend the contemporary programme in very different directions. They are not one new generation of “dark music”. The schedule shows post-punk, EBM, industrial electronics, synth-driven music and club culture overlapping without becoming interchangeable, and the separate stages keep those distinctions visible. The acoustic, ritual and experimental side The Kulturbühne runs its own programme. Of The Wand & The Moon close the stage on Sunday, while Corde Oblique, Cawatana, Darkwood, Paganland, Tears Of Othila, Nemuer, SIAMGDA ꕾ Marie, Supersimmetria and MS Gentur + Sven Phalanx occupy points between neofolk, ritual sound, experimental electronics, ambient and industrial music. Those artists would lose their context between larger electro acts on a main stage. Splitting the site lets NCN stay broad without pretending all of its music is interchangeable. Who plays when Thursday, 3 September – Kulturbühne / Warm-Up 19:00 Doors 20:00 Bagger 258 20:40 MRDTC 21:35 Prager Handgriff 22:30 Tyske Ludder 23:30 DJ Team – quiet aftershow party Friday, 4 September – Amphibühne 15:30 Doors 16:10 Vanguard 17:50 Melotron 20:05 Elinborg 22:45 Girls Under Glass Friday, 4 September – Waldbühne 15:00 Doors 15:30 Extize 17:00 Jesus On Extasy 18:55 Pankow 21:25 L’Âme Immortelle Friday, 4 September – Parkbühne 15:00 Doors 15:30 HORSKH 17:00 Hinfort 18:55 Atlas Bird 21:25 Siglo XX 00:10 Sierra Veins Friday, 4 September – Kulturbühne 15:00 Doors 16:10 Frequen-C & TC75 17:50 Tears Of Othila 20:05 MS Gentur + Sven Phalanx 22:45 Nemuer 00:50 DJ Adler & DJ SPU Manne – quiet aftershow party Friday, 4 September – Lesebühne 15:00 Doors 15:30 M. Kruppe 17:00 Christian von Aster 18:50 Torsten Low 21:00 Jessica Iser Saturday, 5 September – Amphibühne 11:45 Doors 12:20 Ambassador 21 13:40 AD:Key 15:20 Schöngeist 17:30 Menticide 19:45 Samsas Traum / Weena Morloch 22:30 Nik Kershaw Saturday, 5 September – Waldbühne 10:30 Doors 11:50 Aktion: Fiasko 13:00 Strikkland 14:30 The Awakening 16:25 Container 90 18:30 The Beauty Of Gemina 21:00 SKYND Saturday, 5 September – Parkbühne 10:30 Doors 11:50 Rina Pavar 13:00 Ozibut 14:30 SIIE 16:25 Debdepan 18:30 Lovataraxx 21:00 Actors 23:50 Lone Assembly Saturday, 5 September – Kulturbühne 10:30 Doors 12:20 Paganland 13:40 SIAMGDA 15:20 no artist is named in the current schedule 17:30 Darkwood 19:55 Les Chaussers De La Nuit 22:45 Esplendor Geométrico 01:10 DJ Bastard & DJ Tobi – quiet aftershow party Saturday, 5 September – Lesebühne 10:30 Doors 13:00 Torsten Low 16:25 Christian von Aster 18:30 Markus Heitz Sunday, 6 September – Amphibühne 12:00 Doors 12:30 Grundeis 13:40 Junkie Kut 15:15 Intent:Outtake 17:20 Peter Heppner & Band 20:45 Die Krupps Sunday, 6 September – Waldbühne 11:00 Doors 12:00 Beyond Border 13:00 Lovelorn Dolls 14:20 Mildreda 16:10 Sturm Café 19:25 Diary Of Dreams Sunday, 6 September – Parkbühne 11:00 Doors 12:00 Venin Carmin 13:00 Mayflower Madame 14:20 The Foreign Resort 16:10 Winter Severity Index 18:30 Hundreds Sunday, 6 September – Kulturbühne 11:00 Doors 12:30 Cawatana 13:40 Corde Oblique 15:15 Supersimmetria 17:20 Of The Wand & The Moon Sunday, 6 September – Lesebühne 11:00 Doors 13:00 Dirk Bernemann 14:20 Erk Aicrag 16:15 Markus Heitz 18:55 Christian von Aster NCN 19 Warm-Up: 3 September 2026 Festival: 4-6 September 2026 Kulturpark Deutzen Arno-Bahndorf-Straße 12 Deutzen, Germany Day tickets are currently listed at €75 for Friday, Saturday and Sunday, while several categories of weekend tickets are also available through the official NCN shop. The running order shows Troisch’s booking method in practice. A British pop songwriter with a 1980s chart catalogue goes on one stage, Spanish industrial pioneers on another, true-crime industrial performance on a third and neofolk or experimental electronics elsewhere, with none of them redefined to make the combination work. NCN’s identity rests on which strands still make sense for the same audience in the same weekend, not on holding a genre boundary. After nineteen editions that is still a booking question. About Nocturnal Culture Night Nocturnal Culture Night has been staged at Kulturpark Deutzen in Saxony since 2005, when Holger Troisch opened the first edition on a single stage for roughly 300 visitors. The site sits in the village of Deutzen, part of the municipality of Neukieritzsch, about 30 kilometres south of Leipzig, and its wooded amphitheatre and surrounding buildings gave the festival its four-stage layout from 2014 onwards. Troisch has run the event throughout, latterly through NCN Event GmbH in Leipzig, and the programme covers EBM, industrial, post-punk, coldwave, synthpop, neofolk, ritual and experimental electronics side by side rather than in separate weekends, with a Lesebühne carrying readings by German genre authors in parallel with the music. The 2026 line-up reached its present shape after a change at the top of the bill. Marc Almond was announced as the first NCN 19 headliner in September 2025, then withdrew on health grounds; Nik Kershaw was booked in his place for the Saturday Amphibühne slot. Camping and non-camping weekend tickets and day tickets are sold only through the official NCN shop, and caravan and parking tickets sold out earlier in the year. The 2027 edition is the one the organisers count as the twentieth jubilee, which makes NCN 19 the last edition before that anniversary.

items.body: Ministry released “We Hate” on August 21, 2026 through Cleopatra Records, the second single from the industrial band’s final studio album, “Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery)“, due October 30. A video directed by Joshua Bradford premieres the same day at 18:00 Central European Summer Time. The single takes Donald Trump as its subject. A press release from Red Sand PR states that Al Jourgensen and the band “felt it necessary to give ‘Trumplethinskin’ a dose of his own medicine”. Bradford, a former Revolting Cocks bandmate of Jourgensen, also directed the video for “Burned Out”, the album’s first single, issued in July. Where ‘We Hate’ sits on ‘Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery)’ “We Hate” is track four of ten. The album closes with “We’re Still Here”, the only track to feature former Ministry bassist Paul Barker, his only appearance on the record. The rest of it was cut with Jourgensen’s current line-up: guitarists Monte Pittman and Cesar Soto, bassist Paul D’Amour, synth player John Bechdel and drummer Pepe Clarke Magaña. “Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery)” arrives on vinyl in several variants, on CD, on cassette and digitally. Track seven, “The White Man Lied”, appears only on the CD and digital editions and is left off the cassette and vinyl pressings. The full tracklist reads: Crickets Voices of Hate Clown Car We Hate Delete Grifter The White Man Lied Singularity Burned Out We’re Still Here (feat. Paul Barker) Ministry ‘Goodbye Europe 2027’ tour dates The album is followed by a farewell touring cycle. The European leg runs to 21 shows with Die Krupps as special guests, opening in Utrecht on April 2, 2027 and closing in Helsinki on May 1. Meet-and-greet packages sold through soundrink.co include a photo opportunity with Jourgensen, a laminate pass, a silkscreen poster and a European tour coin. April 2, 2027 – Utrecht, Netherlands – Ronda April 3, 2027 – Saarbrücken, Germany – Garage April 4, 2027 – Brussels, Belgium – Ancienne Belgique April 6, 2027 – Manchester, UK – O2 Victoria Warehouse April 7, 2027 – Dublin, Ireland – 3Olympia April 9, 2027 – Nottingham, UK – Rock City April 10, 2027 – London, UK – Troxy April 12, 2027 – Paris, France – Bataclan April 14, 2027 – Madrid, Spain – La Riviera April 15, 2027 – Barcelona, Spain – Paral-lel April 17, 2027 – Lausanne, Switzerland – Docks April 18, 2027 – Munich, Germany – Tonhalle April 19, 2027 – Vienna, Austria – Gasometer April 21, 2027 – Prague, Czech Republic – Forum Karlín April 22, 2027 – Warsaw, Poland – Progresja April 24, 2027 – Berlin, Germany – Columbiahalle April 25, 2027 – Hamburg, Germany – Grosse Freiheit 36 April 26, 2027 – Copenhagen, Denmark – Amager Bio April 27, 2027 – Oslo, Norway – Rockefeller April 29, 2027 – Stockholm, Sweden – Fållan May 1, 2027 – Helsinki, Finland – House of Culture About Ministry Ministry was formed in Chicago in 1981 by Al Jourgensen. The project started with synth-pop material issued as 12-inch singles on the newly founded Wax Trax! Records, followed by the debut album “With Sympathy” on Arista Records in 1983. Jourgensen moved the band toward a harsher, sample-driven sound across “Twitch” (1986), “The Land of Rape and Honey” (1988) and “The Mind Is a Terrible Thing to Taste” (1989), then reached its widest audience with “Psalm 69: The Way to Succeed and the Way to Suck Eggs” (1992), which brought the first of six Grammy nominations. Paul Barker played bass and co-produced through that period and left in 2003. Eight further albums followed before Jourgensen shut the band down in 2013. Ministry returned in 2018 with “AmeriKKKant”, then issued “Moral Hygiene” (2021) and “HOPIUMFORTHEMASSES” (2024). In March 2025 the band released “The Squirrely Years Revisited” on Cleopatra Records, a set of re-recorded songs from its early synth-pop catalogue, and followed it with first-ever official videos for “Everyday Is Halloween” and “I’ll Do Anything For You” and a Jurgen Engler remix of the live track “Dancing Alone” in March 2026. Alongside Ministry, Jourgensen has run Revolting Cocks, Lard, Pailhead and Surgical Meth Machine; Barker returned to recording as Lead Into Gold in 2023. “Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery)” is billed as the band’s 17th and last studio album, and “We Hate” is its second single.
items._cn_summary: 本文为纯新闻稿性质内容，介绍工业金属乐队Ministry发布单曲'We Hate'及其告别专辑'Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery)'的相关信息，包括发行日期、厂牌、曲目列表、巡演安排及主创阵容。专辑以政治讽刺为主题，单曲矛头直指特朗普，延续乐队一贯的工业金属风格，配备电吉他、合成器与鼓机制造的厚重音墙。文章未涉及任何音乐性分析、声音设计讨论或艺术评价，信息仅停留在发行资讯层面。虽工业/EBM属于用户偏好中的暗潮范畴，但内容缺乏乐评深度，且文章性质为新闻通讯而非评论，价值有限。

items.body: Sentient Ruin Laboratories will issue Marca Diaboli’s debut EP “Labyrintomb” on vinyl on September 11, 2026, the first time the five-track record has been pressed. The Oakland label describes the project as a Chilean-Austrian occult rock, post-punk and black metal act, and the EP first appeared on October 31, 2025 as a cassette limited to sixty copies on the German label Sect Entropy. The vinyl is a single-sided 12″ with the B-side silkscreened in metallic gold ink, housed in a matte sleeve printed black inside, with an insert inlay and a download card. Two pressings exist: a crystal clear edition of one hundred copies worldwide, sold direct by the label and not distributed to shops, and a standard black edition. Three of the five test pressings are also being offered, hand-numbered, signed, and packaged in a black fold-over cover silkscreened in gold. “Labyrintomb” runs eighteen minutes across “Digging Graves”, “Nightfalls”, “Arsonists”, “Manifest” and “The Last Nail”. It was recorded and performed by a single musician credited as M.R.C. between May and June 2025 in Lower Austria, with Krsfrs mixing and M.R.C. mastering. Steven Henningsard cut the vinyl master and Svart Graphics handled the cover art and layout. Sentient Ruin calls the EP “a grave-born spell book of primeval shamanic rock musick” and names In Solitude, Negative Plane, Bauhaus, Amebix and The Devil’s Blood as its reference points. The lo-fi production comes out of black metal, but the melodies and the pacing sit closer to post-punk and early-1990s underground rock than to anything in that genre. Labyrintomb by MARCA DIABOLI About Marca Diaboli Marca Diaboli was conceived in the forests of Lower Austria and dates its own founding to 2025. The label’s account puts the project’s first public step in the summer of that year, when the track “Nightfalls” was self-released digitally on Bandcamp, and its debut proper at the end of October 2025 with the “Labyrintomb” cassette on Sect Entropy. The project works as a one-person operation on record: M.R.C. performs everything and shares the credits only with a mixing engineer and the vinyl and artwork staff. No member names have been published beyond those initials, and the Chilean side of the Chilean-Austrian description has not been detailed by the band or the label. Its stated sources are late-1980s and early-1990s underground rock, post-punk and metal, the rawest end of second-wave black metal, and contemporary dark rock. Beyond “Labyrintomb” and the “Nightfalls” single, the project has released nothing else. The September vinyl is its first release for Sentient Ruin, a label that has spent a decade working the edges of black metal, doom, noise and post-punk out of Oakland, California.

items._cn_summary: Marca Diaboli 首张 EP 将卡带格式首次压制为单面黑胶，B面以金属金色丝网印刷，限量一百张水晶透明版本由厂牌直售，不进入分销渠道。整张作品时长十八分钟，由奥地利下奥地利州的一位音乐人独自完成录音与演奏，仅与混音师和母带工程师分享署名。黑胶刻盘由 Steven Henningsard 操刀，封面与版式设计交由 Svart Graphics 负责。制作走低保真路线，旋律与节奏编排更接近后朋克与九十年代初地下摇滚，而非典型黑金属逻辑。Sentient Ruin 将其描述为源自坟墓的萨满摇滚咒语，参考 In Solitude、Negative Plane、Bauhaus、Amebix 与 The Devil's Blood 等乐队。项目以智利-奥地利双重身份自居，但智利一面的来源未被厂牌或乐队进一步说明。除此张 EP 与一支单曲外，该项目暂无其他发行。

items.album: Greg Bullock closes his track-by-track ’26EP’ with ‘Blu-Green Beauty’

items.body: New Jersey dark rock and post-punk musician Greg Bullock has finished “26EP”, a self-released four-track EP he built in public on Bandcamp. The page opened on June 12, 2026 and filled up one song at a time, closing with “Blu-Green Beauty” on August 13, 2026. The running order is “In Other Words” (3:44), “Thirty Pieces” (3:50), “I Ain’t Goin!” (2:21) and “Blu-Green Beauty” (4:56). Bullock wrote, produced, performed and mixed everything himself, playing vocals, hardware and software synthesizers and arranging the drum tracks. He recorded at his own GABWorx, Studio B; Mark Trewella mastered at Full Circle Mastering. The cover and track photos are Bullock’s own. The closing track is the plainest of the four in intent. Bullock sums it up in a single line on its Bandcamp page: “Our world is not the dump that humans treat it as.” The lead track, “In Other Words”, turns on ignorance, persecution and contaminated morality, subjects Bullock has called “ideas we may not want to think about.” The EP is digital and carries no label. Bullock spreads it across goth rock, post-punk, synth rock and a strain of alt-country, so no two of the four tracks sit in quite the same place. Greg Bullock – 26EP by Greg Bullock About Greg Bullock Greg Bullock is a musician and producer based in Plumsted Township, New Jersey, where he runs the GABWorx studio. He is best known as co-founder, vocalist and keyboard player of Cyborg Amok, the duo he started in 2019 with his son Brydon Bullock on drums and vocals. The pair describe that project as gothic-infused synth-rock; their most recent album, “Pins & Needles”, came out in April 2025. Bullock’s solo catalogue runs alongside it and shares the same Bandcamp page, which also carries Brydon’s own tracks. He gathered his earlier work on “Best Of … so far!” in September 2025, then released the standalone single “No Exit” the following month. A second Bandcamp account under the GABWorx name holds the albums “Etiam” and “The Language Angels Speak In The Darkness”. “26EP” is his first multi-track solo release since that 2025 collection, and the first he assembled in the open rather than shipping complete. There is no video for any of the four tracks; the EP is available on Bandcamp and on the streaming services.
items._genre: dark rock / post-punk / synth rock / alt-country
items._cn_summary: 新泽西音乐人格雷格·布洛克以公开制作方式在Bandcamp上逐步推出四首单曲，最终汇成这张自发行EP。所有演奏、编曲、混音均由他独立完成，硬件与软件合成器交织，鼓轨经编程排列。曲目横跨哥特摇滚、后朋克、合成器摇滚乃至另类乡村四种风格基调，每首歌的位置都略有偏移。闭幕曲主题最为直白，聚焦人类对环境的破坏。创作动机涉及冷漠、迫害与受污染的道德等沉重议题。他以家庭工作室为基础，另与儿子合作运营二人组Cyborg Amok，持续在暗潮与合成器摇滚交叉地带探索。整张作品以数字形式分发，无厂牌背景，制作方式公开透明。

items.body: Neapolitan project Fiori del Male released “Allarme rosso nel golfo persico” on April 4, 2026, thirty-five years after Nunzio Ciccone wrote it. The five-minute track sets an anti-war lyric against post-punk guitars, alternative rock instrumentation and electronics, and had sat unreleased since 1991. Ciccone wrote it in Scampia, in the northern outskirts of Naples, while the first Gulf War was being broadcast live. The lyric is about that broadcast rather than the fighting: propaganda, saturation coverage, and what happens when a war arrives in a living room through a television set. Ciccone sings and Andrea Palazzo plays guitar, with Vincenzo Esposito on bass and Claudio Ciccone handling DJ work and production. The New York engineer known as MisterAC mastered it. The single is self-released under the Nunzio Ciccone Bros. imprint and distributed digitally; it is on Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer and YouTube, and there is no physical edition and no music video. About Fiori del Male Fiori del Male formed in Scampia, Naples in the early 1990s around Nunzio Ciccone, who has led it under several names since. The group first worked as Flowers Of Evil, the English rendering of the same phrase, then as FlowerPeace after moving to Milan in 1998. In 2000 the members relocated to London and stayed there until 2012, writing and recording in the city for twelve years before returning to Naples in 2014. The project is now spread between Rome, London and Naples, and works as a collective rather than a fixed lineup: Ciccone, his siblings Claudio and Alessia Ciccone, and a rotating set of players including Palazzo and Esposito. Recorded output has been sparse. The single “E’ solo un giorno che non va, con la luna dentro gli occhi” appeared on April 30, 2020, credited to Ciccone with Alessia Ciccone, Vincenzo Esposito, Armando Vertullo, Danilo Napoli, Roberto Zincone and Fiori del Male. “Angeli Ribelli” followed on July 31, 2023. “Allarme rosso nel golfo persico” is the third release under the name in six years, and the oldest piece of writing among them by a wide margin. Note for readers searching for the project: a separate Italian black metal duo from Brindisi also records as Fiori del Male, and several streaming services merge the two into one artist page. They are unrelated.
items._cn_summary: 意大利那不勒斯Scampia出身的Fiori del Male在2026年4月发行了单曲《Allarme rosso nel golfo persico》，这首歌由主创Nunzio Ciccone在1991年海湾战争期间写成，但搁置了三十五年才正式发布。五分钟的后朋克吉他与另类摇滚器乐搭配电子元素，歌词聚焦于电视直播中的宣传饱和与战争在客厅里的呈现，而非战争本身本身。乐队由Ciccone、Andrea Palazzo（吉他）、Vincenzo Esposito（贝斯）和Claudio Ciccone（DJ与制作）组成，自行在Nunzio Ciccone Bros.厂牌下数字发行，无实体版本也无MV。乐队历史横跨那不勒斯、米兰、伦敦三地，以集体模式运作，此前仅有两首零星发行。整篇文章偏新闻稿性质，未对音乐本身的声响设计或歌词深度展开评论。

items.body: KMFDM, the industrial and EBM group led by Sascha Konietzko, released “Tohuvabohu” on 21 August 2007 through Metropolis Records and the band’s own KMFDM Records. The album turns 19 this year. It ran to eleven tracks on CD and arrived between “Hau Ruck” in 2005 and “Blitz” in 2009. The title comes from the biblical Hebrew phrase “tohu va bohu”, meaning “without form and void”; KMFDM Records described the word as meaning “wild and chaotic”. How KMFDM recorded ‘Tohuvabohu’ in Seattle Konietzko and Jules Hodgson produced the album. The band recorded at Kommandozentrale and The Black Lab Studio in Seattle, mixed at Chicago Recording Company in Chicago and again at Kommandozentrale, and Brian Gardner mastered it at Bernie Grundman Mastering in Hollywood. The line-up was Konietzko on vocals, analogue synthesizers, bass and programming, Lucia Cifarelli on vocals, Hodgson on guitar, bass, synthesizer and programming, Steve White on guitar, synthesizer and programming, and Andy Selway on drums and programming. Amy Denio added alto saxophone to the opening track and Jim Knodle played trumpet on it. The eleven tracks are “Superpower”, “Looking For Strange”, “Tohuvabohu”, “I Am What I Am”, “Saft Und Kraft”, “Headcase”, “Los Niños Del Parque”, “Not In My Name”, “Spit Or Swallow”, “Fait Accompli” and “Bumaye”. Two tracks carry outside material. “Superpower” is built around recordings made by KMFDM listeners, who called a phone line the band set up and taped what the group meant to them; further calls from the same line surfaced a year later as “What We Do For You” on the companion remix album “Brimborium”. “Los Niños Del Parque” is a cover of the Liaisons Dangereuses track written by Beate Bartel, Chrislo Haas and Krishna Goineau, and is the one song on the record not credited to the band. The sleeve produced a public disagreement. Aidan Hughes, who works as Brute! and has drawn almost every KMFDM cover since 1987, posted to his blog in June 2007 that he was unhappy with the changes made to his submitted artwork: the red palette had been switched to orange, and the stylised buildings and cranes in the background had been replaced with a starburst. Metropolis Records reissued the album as a remastered digital edition in 2012. Tohuvabohu by KMFDM About KMFDM KMFDM began in Paris on 29 February 1984, as a performance art project between Sascha Konietzko and the German painter and multimedia artist Udo Sturm, staged at the opening of an exhibition of young European artists at the Grand Palais. Sturm played an ARP 2600 synthesizer, Konietzko played bass guitars through amplifiers spread through the building, and four Polish coal miners pounded on the building’s foundations. The name is an initialism of the deliberately ungrammatical German phrase Kein Mehrheit Für Die Mitleid, usually given the loose translation “no pity for the majority”. Konietzko has called the band’s music “The Ultra-Heavy Beat”. Sturm left early. Konietzko returned to Hamburg and joined Peter Missing in Missing Foundation, where he met drummer Nicklaus Schandelmaier, who took the stage name En Esch. The two left Missing Foundation before any recordings were made and resumed work as KMFDM with the Hamburg studio owner Raymond Watts. The debut album “What Do You Know, Deutschland?” appeared in December 1986, assembled from sessions running back to 1983, some of them cut by Konietzko and Watts before Esch joined. Skysaw Records gave it a second UK release in 1987, which brought Aidan Hughes to the band; he redesigned that cover and stayed. Watts worked on three songs for “Don’t Blow Your Top” in 1988, then left to start PIG. That album was licensed to Wax Trax! Records for US distribution, and “UAIOE” followed in 1989. The band signed directly to Wax Trax! for “Naïve” in 1990, which introduced guitarist Günter Schulz. Konietzko moved to Chicago in 1991 and Esch followed a year later; “Money” came in 1992 and “Angst” in 1993. Konietzko relocated to Seattle in 1994, and in late 1995 the city became the band’s official headquarters. Watts rejoined for “Nihil” in 1995, which sold roughly 209,000 copies, the band’s best-selling album; Bill Rieflin played drums. “Xtort” in 1996 reached No. 92, the band’s highest chart placing, and Esch returned for “Symbols” in 1997, the year Tim Skold joined. KMFDM broke up on 22 January 1999, with only Konietzko and Skold remaining. “Adios” arrived three months later and reached No. 189 on the Billboard 200. Schulz and Esch formed Slick Idiot; Konietzko and Skold regrouped as MDFMK with singer Lucia Cifarelli and released one album through Republic/Universal. Konietzko announced KMFDM’s return in early 2001, citing public demand, and “Attak” followed in March 2002 on Metropolis Records. Skold left after it to join Marilyn Manson. Selway first played drums on “WWIII” in 2003, the last album Watts performed on, and White contributed to “Hau Ruck” in 2005. The demo album “Opium” was reissued in 2002 as the first release on KMFDM Records, and Metropolis reissued the Wax Trax!-era studio catalogue in pairs and threes between September 2006 and May 2007. “Tohuvabohu” closed that stretch. Two months after it came out, Konietzko announced he was moving back to Germany within three months; Cifarelli went with him while the rest of the band stayed in the United States. “Brimborium” followed in 2008, then “Blitz” in 2009, “WTF?!” in 2011, “Kunst” in 2013 and “Our Time Will Come” in 2014. White and Hodgson were unavailable for “Hell Yeah” in 2017, so Chris Harms of Lord Of The Lost recorded the guitar parts; when Lord Of The Lost could not obtain US work visas for the supporting tour, Andee Blacksugar took the touring guitar role and stayed until 2025. “Paradise” was released on 27 September 2019, with Watts guesting for the first time since 2003, followed by “Hyëna” on 9 September 2022 and “Let Go” on 2 February 2024, which marked forty years since the Grand Palais show. Esch, meanwhile, returned to his own catalogue, reported here in En Esch returns with first album in eight years: ‘Dance Hall Putsch’. The band’s current record is “Enemy”, announced in KMFDM announce new album ‘Enemy’ on Metropolis Records and trailed by the remix covered in KMFDM releases ‘Enemy (Inhalt Geld ’88 Remix)’. The European tour built around it was pushed back, as reported in KMFDM postpone 2026 European tour, will still release ‘Enemy’. Nineteen years on, “Tohuvabohu” stands as the last KMFDM album completed before Konietzko left Seattle for Germany.
items._cn_summary: 这是KMFDM 2007年专辑《Tohuvabohu》发行19周年的回顾性文章，主要以信息陈述为主。文章详细介绍了专辑的录制过程、制作团队、十一首曲目列表以及乐手阵容。专辑由Konietzko和Hodgson在西雅图制作，混音在芝加哥完成，母带处理在好莱坞进行。制作中融入了听众电话录音作为创作素材，封面设计因色彩变更引发了与长期合作艺术家Aidan Hughes的公开分歧。专辑名称源自希伯来语短语，意为'无形与空虚'。整体内容为事实性记录而非深度乐评，缺乏对音乐风格、声响设计或艺术价值的批判性分析。作为工业和EBM类型作品，KMFDM在该领域具有代表性，但文章本身的评论深度有限，多为档案性质的资料整理。

items.body:
Kurt Wagner's seventeeth album as Lambchop - drawing on gospel and centuries-old Scots-Appalachian call-and-response singing.

"Lambchop's seventeenth album Punching the Clown finds Kurt Wagner returning to first principles. Sparked by a late-night radio encounter with an unidentified gospel recording, Wagner fell deep into the world of "lined out singing" a centuries-old Scots-Appalachian call-and-response tradition in which a lone clerk leads a choir through hymns, word by unadorned word. That spirit of raw, communal voice shapes every moment of Punching the Clown: Wagner spent years studying great songwriters and relearning his craft from the ground up, whittling dozens of songs down to twelve. Recorded in three days with guitarist Andrew Broder, Justin Vernon on banjo, and a six-part choir assembled by Blake Morgan and engineered by Lambchop veteran Mark Nevers, the album is graceful, wry, and quietly devastating. Out August 21, 2026 on City Slang.

Produced by Ryan Olson and recorded August 25–27, 2025, at April Base, Wisconsin. The record was completed over three days and features Kurt Wagner (vocals), Andrew Broder (guitar), Justin Vernon (banjo), and a six-part vocal ensemble, with additional choir recordings in London and Minneapolis."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Lambchop的第十七张录音室作品，Kurt Wagner受深夜电台中一段无名福音录音启发，深入钻研“lined out singing”这一古老的苏格兰-阿巴拉契亚呼应歌唱传统。他花费数年研究词曲创作并重新打磨手艺，将大量歌曲缩减为十二首。专辑在三天内录制完成，由Andrew Broder担任吉他、Justin Vernon演奏班卓琴，并辅以六人合唱团，制作由Ryan Olson操刀，录音地点为威斯康星州的April Base。整体上，作品围绕人声与合唱展开，呈现出优雅、诙谐而含蓄沉重的气质，回归了以质朴人声为核心的创作本源。

items.body:
More than five decades after its debut, Jesus Christ Superstar still knows how to make an entrance.

The Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice rock opera arrives at Sands Theatre, Marina Bay Sands for its Singapore season from 19 August to 6 September, bringing with it the Olivier Award-winning Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre production that has toured the UK, North America, Australia, Manila and Hong Kong.

But anyone expecting robes, sandals and a conventional Biblical epic should adjust their expectations. Director Timothy Sheader’s production strips the story down and plugs it straight into the electricity of a rock concert: handheld microphones, industrial scaffolding, streetwear, piercing lights and a live band turn the Passion of Christ into something urgent, physical and startlingly contemporary.

It is loud. It is restless. And, at its best, it is deeply human.

The musical has always approached its familiar story from an unusual angle. Rather than simply retelling the final days of Jesus Christ, it places Judas Iscariot at the centre of the conflict, watching with alarm as his friend and leader becomes an increasingly powerful public figure.

That tension is what gives this production its pulse.

Javon King, as Judas, attacks the role with seemingly endless nervous energy. He prowls the stage, lashes out and throws himself into Rice's rapid-fire lyrics as though trying to reason his way out of a disaster he can already see coming. Judas is not reduced to a straightforward villain here; he is frightened, frustrated and increasingly desperate, convinced that the movement around Jesus has grown beyond anyone's control.

Opposite him, Luke Street gives Jesus a compelling vulnerability. His Messiah is not an untouchable icon but a leader steadily buckling beneath expectation — surrounded by followers, yet increasingly isolated from them.

That makes 'Gethsemane' the inevitable emotional peak. Lloyd Webber's notoriously demanding number asks Jesus to move through anger, terror, exhaustion and acceptance in a matter of minutes, and Street turns it into something closer to an exposed nerve than a conventional musical-theatre showstopper.

That push and pull between celebrity and humanity is where this staging feels particularly alive.

When Jesus' followers surround him, the imagery could almost belong to a modern concert: a charismatic figure at the centre of an adoring crowd, microphones in hand, bodies constantly moving around him. Drew McOnie's muscular choreography adds to the sensation, transforming the ensemble from disciples to fans to mob with unsettling ease.

The live band, positioned within Tom Scutt's industrial design, only reinforces that concert-like quality. Steel structures frame a cross-shaped platform while Lee Curran's lighting shifts between the glare of a stadium performance and something darker and more ominous.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by BASE ENTERTAINMENT ASIA (@baseasia)

It can occasionally feel deliberately overwhelming. The choreography rarely sits still, while the production's abstract visual language asks audiences to keep pace with a story told entirely through song. For those unfamiliar with Jesus Christ Superstar or the Passion narrative, the first act in particular can demand close attention.

But that relentless momentum also pays off. By the second half, the spectacle begins to contract around Jesus. The crowds, lights and movement that once signified adoration gradually become instruments of intimidation and violence.

Even the production's more unusual visual ideas gather weight as the evening progresses. Silver and gold are not simply decorative flourishes; they become bound up with betrayal, money and punishment. The crucifixion, meanwhile, is all the more striking because the production resists turning it into traditional religious pageantry.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by BASE ENTERTAINMENT ASIA (@baseasia)

Around Street and King is a company that embraces the score's theatrical extremes.

Grant Hodges makes Caiaphas an imposing presence, his cavernous lower register cutting through the production's wall of sound, while Kodiak Thompson gives Annas a more wiry menace. Ethan Hardy Benson brings a cold authority to Pontius Pilate, while Erich W. Schleck gets one of the night's most delicious changes of pace with the flamboyant 'King Herod's Song'.

Singapore also gives this international production a distinctly local presence through Tabitha Nauser and Frances Lee, who share the role of Mary Magdalene during the season. Amid a score filled with confrontation and distortion, Mary provides some of its rare moments of stillness, particularly through 'I Don't Know How to Love Him' and 'Could We Start Again Please'.

It is an important counterweight. For all the production's rock-star swagger, Jesus Christ Superstar works because its characters are allowed to be frightened, jealous, confused and uncertain.

That was part of the musical's provocation when Rice and Lloyd Webber first released it as a concept album in 1970, and it remains its strength today. This is less interested in telling audiences what to believe than in asking what happens to people when faith, politics, ambition and fame become impossible to separate.

Sheader's production pushes that idea even further. Its Jesus could be a musician overwhelmed by his own following. Its Judas could be the friend watching success turn into something dangerous. Its disciples could be devotees whose adoration can transform into fury almost overnight.

More than 50 years on, that feels less like an update imposed upon Jesus Christ Superstar than proof of how elastic the musical has always been. Beneath the scaffolding, glitter and screaming guitars is an old story about people struggling with loyalty, power and the consequences of their choices. And when all that noise finally disappears, it is the silence that hits hardest.

Tickets are priced from SGD 58 to SGD 188, excluding booking fees, with dynamic pricing applying. Tickets are available via Marina Bay Sands Ticketing, SISTIC, Klook, and Singtel.

The international tour of Jesus Christ Superstar is produced by David Ian for Crossroads Live and Work Light Productions. The Singapore season is presented by Base Entertainment Asia under the direction of Chantal Prudhomme.

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — Exit founder and leader Al Kooper (turning toward the production and A&R side of Columbia Records), here today is power vocalist David Clayton-Thomas. Other members remaining from the debut album include the excellent rhythm corps of bassist Jim Fielder, drummer Bobby Colomby, and guitarist Steve Katz as well as sax player Fred Lipsius and trombonist Dick Halligan (who now has added piano, flute, and organ to his The album was recorded in New York City at Columbia's 30th Street Studios ("The Church") during the span of October 7-22, 1968 and then released at the end of the year from where it dominated the charts, holding the #1 spot for six weeks in 1969, spawning three hit singles to each reach #2: "You've Made Me So Very Happy," "Spinning Wheel," and "And When I Die" before winning the 1970 Grammy Award for Album of the Year.1. "Variations On A Theme By Erik Satie (1st and 2nd Movements)" * (2:30) performed rather faithfully by Steve Katz providing the chords normally left to the piano's left hand on his classical guitar with flutes, and/or recorders tracking the main melody up top--until, that is, until the tinkling of a percussionists winde chimes signals a bridge to a fully meted out Brass Rock version (the "2nd Movement") varying the notes and chords with highly-treated (flanged) drums, bass, and loud horn section. Interesting! (9.125/10)2. "Smiling Phases" (5:10) a song that really puts on full display the band's power and enthusiastic energy while also introducing their powerful new vocalist, David Clayton-Thomas. After 90 seconds, the band launches into an impressive jazzy instrumental section in which bass player Jim Fielder, drummer Bobby Colomby show their skills as the horns and Fred Lipsius' piano show off their skills over what turns out to be a two-part movement: the first fast, the second slow and protracted, before returning to the opening motif for David and the band to finish with the same energy as they opened with to bookend the song. Nice! (9/10)3. "Sometimes In Winter "(3:08) smooth, beautiful, fully-orchestrated music with the smooth vocal of Steve Katz, the band finds themselves creating more of that Jimmy Webb folkie, anachronistic Baroque Pop that is so pleasing to the ear. I like this song very much. Steve Katz could definitely have had a career as a singer: he sounds like a cross between a certain member of The Association and Bobby Darren. (9.25/10)4. "More and More" (3:04) picking up where "Smiling Phases" left off (though David's voice is mixed a little more deeply into the soundscape than before). More creative uses for the horn section to inject their accents into the mix (substituting for the B.B. King-like blues guitar riffs). Jim and Bobby bring it with such amazing energy and skill! The futuristic (Frippian) guitar tone used by Steve Katz in the solo toward the end of the second minute, during the organ-based instrumental mid-section, is quite cool (and loud)! Incredibly tight and powerful musicianship on this complex tune. (9.125/10)5. "And When I Die" (4:05) the hit cover of Laura Nyro's song, the song is notable for its dynamic shift between its sparse, dirge-like harmonica opening, the ensuing easy-going circus-music-like verses and the way the music turns to vaudeville-Western-showtune-like as they go on. And then there are the dramatically-held suspension of the song's title in the chorus and unusual pauses. Very much like something one would see on a Broadway musical. The faithful rendering of a rather complicated composition is the most impressive part for me (on a song that I've never really been very high on). (9/10)6. "God Bless The Child" (5:56) another song that feels stage-worthy (which makes sense since it was composed by Arthur Herzog, Jr. and Billie Holiday). In a very interesting (and totally unexpected) twist, at 3:06 the song turns into a Afro-Cubano-flavored piano- and percussion-based jam for the horn players to really stretch out: both collectively and each, individually. But then at 4:24 the song comes back to its origins (though with noticeably more forceful horns, more organ, and the joinder of a bluesy harmonica, which weren't so prevalent in the opening). Ballsy but these guys are definitely up to the challenge. (9.125/10)7. "Spinning Wheel" (4:07) one of those memorable brainworm songs, this one composed by newcomer David Clayton-Thomas. The horns were always my favorite part though David is solid (and even able to show some sensitivity). Definitely the most interchangeable song with the other Brass Rock pioneer, CHICAGO (Transit Authority). The instrumental section in the middle (which is sometimes cut out for radio play) is pretty cool--as is the finale with it's horn blasts, great drumming, and calliope-like recorder play. (9/10)8. "You've Made Me So Very Happy" (4:19) the album's first single release, it was borrowed from the Motown catalogue having been covered by one of its authors, Brenda Holloway in a mildly-successful 1967 release as a 45 rpm single (the final arrangement of which Ms. Holloway fought hard to control, a battle she ultimately lost--which led to her leaving Motown/Tamla). BS&T's version was a massive chart topper that remains memorable and emotionally relevant to this day. I am most impressed by David Clayton-Thomas' ability to tone it down and soften his delivery for the tender, sensitive verses. (9.25/10)9. "Blues-Part II" (11:45) an instrumental epic that opens with organ, bass, drums, all of which are quite simple and rudimentary (which is greatly disappointing considering the absolutely jaw-dropping skills the band's rhythm section has shown in the super-tight, super demanding arrangements of all their vocal songs). By the time the fifth minute rolls around the band has finally settled into something more meaty (though, ironically, it's a two-chord vamp) over which Fred Lipsius performs a long multi-part solo on his alto sax: at first over the fast-tempo vamp but then equally-impactful over the slowed down for the seventh and eighth minutes. How humorous is it that the band (Jim Fielder) chooses the "Sunshine of Your Love"/"In-a-gadda-da-vida" bass line to open and carry the next section. Luckily, he lets go of it at 8:40, whereupon the band transitions into a purely-Blues motif over which David sings in a genuinely-feeling blues tradition as Steve Katz tries to project a Blues guitar tone and style while Bobby bashes away on the drum kit beneath and the horn section slowly ramps up their intensity--until someone in the production booth decided to pull the plug: they slowly fade the song out even while David is launching into a classic Wilson Pickett lyric with increasing power and emotion! (22/25)10. "Variations On A Theme By Erik Satie (1st Movement)" * (1:37) a replication of the opening movement from the beginning of the album, this time ending before the Brass Rock rendering starts--with the sound of a door slamming shut! (4.75/5)* Adapted from Satie's "Trois Gymnop�dies"Total time 45:41A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of genre-leading Brass Rock. Though I am nowhere near as much a fan of this album as their debut, I recognize the superior craftsmanship that went into the rendering of each and every song and cannot imagine denying it it's deserved masterpiece status.
